So there’s all these kind of basic properties of a person that are indexed in a voice.
paras.zh: 布莱恩特：线索是任何可以预测发送者某些信息的属性。例如，您可以通过听声音来判断一个人有多大。一般通过听声音就可以判断他们是男性还是女性。你能看出他们是老是年轻，对吧？因此，一个人的所有这些基本属性都可以在声音中索引。

paras.en: Sanders: Voices can carry emotions too. A smile, for example, has subtle sound cues.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：声音也可以承载情感。例如，微笑就有微妙的声音提示。

paras.en: Bryant: There’s a slight increase in pitch when you smile and then you change what are called formants. The formants are structures in the speech signal underlying what your perception of vowels is. They’re energy bands that are associated with resonating chambers in your throat and in your mouth. And so when you are moving your tongue around and changing your lips and doing other things going, ahowowowow, you’re changing the formants. That’s the resonating bands of energy in the voice. So when you smile, then the formants change a little bit. And it’s detectable. It’s subtle, but you can hear it for sure.
paras.zh: 布莱恩特：当你微笑时，音高会略有增加，然后你会改变所谓的共振峰。共振峰是语音信号中的结构，它是您对元音的感知的基础。它们是与喉咙和口腔中的共振室相关的能量带。因此，当您移动舌头、改变嘴唇以及做其他事情时，哇哇哇，您正在改变共振峰。这就是声音中能量的共振带。所以当你微笑时，共振峰会发生一些变化。而且它是可以检测到的。虽然很微妙，但你肯定能听到。

paras.en: Sanders: See if you can detect it here. It’s Jules introducing an episode of their podcast in 2020.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：看看你能不能在这里检测到它。 Jules 正在介绍他们 2020 年播客的一集。

paras.en: [podcast] So my wife comes to me today, and she says, babe, I have diarrhea.
paras.zh: [播客] 所以我的妻子今天来找我，她说，宝贝，我腹泻了。

paras.en: Sanders: So setting aside the content he chose to share, which was a bold choice, you can hear the grin in his voice.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：所以抛开他选择分享的内容（这是一个大胆的选择），你可以听到他声音中的笑容。

paras.en: [podcast] Before we get into that, though, I also want to say one quick thing. Happy birthday, my love.
paras.zh: [播客] 不过，在我们开始讨论之前，我还想快速说一件事。生日快乐，我的爱人。

paras.en: Sanders: That’s because his smile pulled his lips slightly upward and changed the shape of the air coming out, thereby changing the sound of his voice. All of these signals in the voice exist because voices are made by bodies. Bodies that move, smile, change, grow older, get sick. Our voices are actually a stunningly sophisticated bit of biology.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：那是因为他的微笑将嘴唇稍微向上拉，改变了空气的形状，从而改变了他的声音。声音中的所有这些信号之所以存在，是因为声音是由身体发出的。身体会移动、微笑、变化、变老、生病。我们的声音实际上是生物学中极其复杂的一部分。

paras.en: Jessica Pietrowski: You think about how, you know, we’re just talking, we’re just voicing, we’re barely even thinking about what we’re doing, but actually upwards close to a hundred muscles are being used.
paras.zh: 杰西卡·皮特罗斯基：你想想，你知道，我们只是在说话，我们只是在发声，我们几乎没有想到我们在做什么，但实际上有近一百块肌肉正在被使用。

paras.en: Sanders: That’s speech-language pathologist and scientist Jessica Pietrowski of UC Davis.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：这是加州大学戴维斯分校的言语病理学家和科学家杰西卡·皮特罗斯基。

paras.en: Pietrowski: When we go to voice, we have to take a breath. Breath comes up, the diaphragm is contracting to get that breath. Breath comes up below the vocal folds, these tissues here, vibrates the vocal folds, creates a tone. That tone comes up through the oral cavity and other spaces, and resonates. And then you have to articulate it, and, and make the sounds clear and sharp. And then you have speech. And so really, you know, we’re not thinking about this as we’re doing it, but it’s incredibly complex and intricate and really an incredible human feat.
paras.zh: Pietrowski：当我们使用声音时，我们必须喘口气。呼吸上升，横膈膜收缩以呼吸。呼吸从声带下方上升，这些组织振动声带，产生音调。这种音调通过口腔和其他空间传出，并产生共鸣。然后你必须清晰地表达出来，并且让声音清晰锐利。然后你就可以讲话了。所以说真的，你知道，我们在做这件事的时候并没有考虑到这一点，但它是极其复杂和错综复杂的，确实是一项令人难以置信的人类壮举。

paras.en: Sanders: Right now, as I say these words to you, I’m pushing air out of my body and using my muscles to move my diaphragm, face, throat, and mouth to make tiny ripples of sound shaped with a precision far below the level of my conscious perception. This mechanical, biological, physical feat is what allows me to shape air into sounds that then move to your ears.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：现在，当我对你说这些话时，我正在将空气从体内推出，并用我的肌肉移动我的隔膜、面部、喉咙和嘴巴，以远远低于我意识感知水平的精度形成微小的声音涟漪。这种机械、生物、物理的壮举使我能够将空气塑造成声音，然后传送到你的耳朵。

paras.en: Sergey Stavisky: So this is a very engineering-y perspective, but one thing about voices, it is our fastest means to communicate what we’re thinking.
paras.zh: 谢尔盖·斯塔维斯基：所以这是一个非常工程化的视角，但关于声音的一件事是，它是我们传达我们想法的最快方式。

paras.en: Sanders: Sergey Stavisky co-directs the UC Davis Neuroprosthetics Lab, focused on using technology to replace or repair parts of the damaged nervous system.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：谢尔盖·斯塔维斯基（Sergey Stavisky）是加州大学戴维斯分校神经假体实验室的共同负责人，该实验室专注于使用技术来替换或修复受损神经系统的部分。

paras.en: Stavisky: So it’s actually, if you step back, kind of magical. So you have some idea in your mind, and your brain is able to take that idea, form it into language. So that’s already a complicated step. And then it’s able to move almost a hundred muscles in your tongue, in your jaw, and in your larynx to vibrate air in this exquisitely precise way.
paras.zh: 斯塔维斯基：所以，如果你退一步看，这实际上有点神奇。所以你脑子里有一些想法，你的大脑能够接受这个想法，将其转化为语言。所以这已经是一个复杂的步骤了。然后它能够​​移动你舌头、下巴和喉部的近一百块肌肉，以这种极其精确的方式振动空气。

paras.en: Sanders: But then, even more magic happens when those vibrations move into someone else’s ear.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：但是，当这些振动进入别人的耳朵时，更多的魔力就会发生。

paras.en: Stavisky: Those vibrations are going to fly through the air and they’re going to hit someone else’s eardrum and it’s going to vibrate that, and it’s going to vibrate the hair cells. And it’s going to send a bunch of nerve signals to their brain and they’re going to first make sense of the sounds you’re making amidst all of the other sounds, whether there’s background conversation or a train rumbling by or a dog barking. But then beyond that, they’re going to not just hear the words you just said, but remember all the previous words, put them together and like get the same idea in their brain. I mean, it’s telepathy through mechanical means.
paras.zh: 斯塔维斯基：这些振动会在空气中飞翔，它们会撞击别人的耳膜，耳膜会振动，毛细胞也会振动。它将向他们的大脑发送一堆神经信号，他们将首先理解你在所有其他声音中发出的声音，无论是背景对话、火车隆隆驶过还是狗吠。但除此之外，他们不仅会听到你刚才说的话，还会记住之前的所有单词，将它们放在一起，就像在他们的大脑中得到相同的想法。我的意思是，这是通过机械手段进行心灵感应。

paras.en: Sanders: Telepathy through mechanical means. When you step back and think about it, it’s an absolute marvel. So here I am floating these ripples out toward my microphone. And then through more technology, they are reaching you, where your own amazing machinery senses those ripples and turns them into meaning. So with these ripples, I’m putting something into your mind.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：通过机械手段进行心灵感应。当你退后一步思考时，这绝对是一个奇迹。所以我在这里将这些涟漪飘向我的麦克风。然后通过更多的技术，它们会到达你身边，你自己神奇的机器会感知到这些涟漪并将其转化为意义。因此，通过这些涟漪，我将一些东西放入你的脑海中。

paras.en: Stavisky: We have this like shared scaffolding of understanding where I can pretty much visualize anything I want and with enough words, make someone else put that into their mind. And I think that’s a really remarkable ability. And that’s like the basis of civilization and learning and science and connection.
paras.zh: 斯塔维斯基：我们有一个共享的理解框架，我几乎可以想象我想要的任何东西，并用足够的语言让其他人将其放入他们的脑海中。我认为这是一种非常了不起的能力。这就像文明、学习、科学和联系的基础。

paras.en: Sanders: But there’s something happening before all of this muscle moving and air rippling, and it’s something that Stavisky just mentioned. My words first started taking shape somewhere else. They started in my brain. Certain clusters of my synapses fired as I thought about what to say. This intricate path from brain to muscles to sculpted air is behind every word we say.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：但是在所有这些肌肉移动和空气波动之前发生了一些事情，这就是斯塔维斯基刚才提到的。我的话首先在其他地方开始成形。它们开始在我的脑海里。当我思考该说什么时，我的某些突触簇会放电。我们所说的每一个字背后都有这条从大脑到肌肉再到雕刻空气的复杂路径。

paras.en: Casey Harrell: Hello there and thanks for being patient with me as I was running a bit late.
paras.zh: 凯西·哈勒尔：您好，感谢您对我的耐心，因为我有点晚了。

paras.en: Sanders: When I met Casey Harrell on Zoom, I asked him to tell me a little bit about himself.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：当我在 Zoom 上见到凯西·哈雷尔时，我请他告诉我一些关于他自己的事情。

paras.en: Casey: That is both the easiest and the hardest question to answer, right? So my name is Casey Harrell, and I am 47 years old. I grew up in the Atlanta area and have lived in the Bay Area for the past 23 years, most of them with my wife, Levana, and our seven-year-old daughter, who is going on 17. I spent most of my professional career as a climate campaigner and have went all over the globe, fighting companies who are destroying the earth and trying to bring some justice to our planet and the people who inhabit it.
paras.zh: 凯西：这是最简单也是最难回答的问题，对吧？我叫凯西·哈勒尔，今年 47 岁。我在亚特兰大地区长大，过去 23 年一直住在湾区，其中大部分时间是和我的妻子 Levana 以及我们即将满 17 岁的 7 岁女儿一起度过的。我职业生涯的大部分时间都是作为气候活动家，并走遍了全球，与破坏地球的公司作斗争，并试图为我们的星球和居住在地球上的人们伸张正义。

paras.en: Sanders: Like Jules, Casey has ALS. The disease has taken a lot from him. He can no longer move most of his body. That includes speech muscles.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：像朱尔斯一样，凯西也患有肌萎缩侧索硬化症。疾病夺去了他的很多生命。他的大部分身体已经无法移动。这包括言语肌肉。

paras.en: Casey: I began to lose my ability to talk shortly after my diagnosis in 2020.
paras.zh: 凯西：2020 年确诊后不久，我就开始失去说话的能力。

paras.en: Sanders: With time, he could no longer talk clearly enough to be understood.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：随着时间的推移，他的讲话不再清晰得让人听懂。

paras.en: Casey: Then it became a slow-motion car crash of multiple years before almost no one would be able to understand me. A few other friends who were around often would be able to understand some of what I was saying. I relied upon my assistant and my wife to basically serve as my translators to other people. I did not go anywhere, even a video call without them, either one or both.
paras.zh: 凯西：然后它变成了一场多年的慢动作车祸，直到几乎没有人能够理解我。其他一些经常在附近的朋友应该能够理解我在说什么。我基本上依靠我的助手​​和我的妻子充当我向其他人提供翻译的工作。我没有去任何地方，甚至在没有他们的情况下进行视频通话，无论是其中一个还是两个。

paras.en: Sanders: Casey’s life in the Bay Area was changing in difficult, almost impossible ways. Like Jules, Casey had received an ALS diagnosis in 2020. Like Jules, he had a kid, a partner, a career, a big, full life. And then wham, life threw them one of the biggest curveballs you can imagine. These two men, separated by 3,000 miles, Jules in Miami, Casey in Oakland, were both facing big losses. And one of the biggest of all was their ability to talk.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：凯西在湾区的生活正在以艰难、几乎不可能的方式发生变化。和朱尔斯一样，凯西在 2020 年被诊断出肌萎缩侧索硬化症。和朱尔斯一样，他也有一个孩子、一个伴侣、一份事业、一个充实而充实的生活。然后砰的一声，生活给了他们一个你能想象到的最大的曲线球。这两个人相距 3,000 英里，朱尔斯在迈阿密，凯西在奥克兰，都面临着巨大的损失。其中最重要的一点就是他们的说话能力。

paras.en: Speech-language pathologist Kate Nilson walks me through some of the standard approaches that she uses when she’s working with people who face similar futures. There’s a process called voice banking.
paras.zh: 言语病理学家凯特·尼尔森向我介绍了她在与面临相似未来的人一起工作时使用的一些标准方法。有一个称为语音银行的流程。

paras.en: Nilson: So voice banking is the idea of recording specific sentences that you might not actually say in real life, but predetermined sentences that you record that give the software the combinations of sounds that it needs to make a computer voice that sounds like you.
paras.zh: 尼尔森：因此，语音银行的想法是记录您在现实生活中实际上可能不会说的特定句子，而是记录您录制的预定句子，这些句子为软件提供了发出听起来像您的计算机声音所需的声音组合。

paras.en: Sanders: That process has actually improved quite a bit in recent years.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：近年来，这个过程实际上有了很大改进。

paras.en: Nilson: When I started doing this, it was 1600 sentences. Now it can be an app on your phone that you do at home. It can be a website that you go to. The software that I use most of the time is 50 sentences. It can be done in like 15 minutes. It’s really come a long way and the voices are pretty darn amazing in how how true to the person they are. But they are still a computerized voice, right? They’re they’re they’re taking combinations of sounds and splicing them together. So it sounds computerized.
paras.zh: Nilson：当我开始这样做时，有 1600 个句子。现在它可以是您在家中使用的手机应用程序。它可以是您访问的网站。我最常使用的软件是50句。大约 15 分钟内即可完成。这确实已经取得了很大的进步，而且这些声音对于他们的真实性来说是非常惊人的。但它们仍然是计算机化的声音，对吗？他们正在将声音组合起来并将它们拼接在一起。所以听起来是电脑化的。

paras.en: Sanders: Voice banking has the benefit of being flexible. This voice can say anything a person wants, but it sounds off. There’s another approach. This one’s called message banking.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：语音银行的优点是灵活。这个声音可以说任何人想说的话，但听起来不太对劲。还有另一种方法。这就是所谓的消息银行。

paras.en: Nilson: So the idea of message banking is we just record an entire message. So instead of using that computer voice to say, “Good night, honey, I love you,” we can just record someone saying, “Good night, honey, I love you,” with their voice, like, with their true inflection and meaning.
paras.zh: 尼尔森：所以消息银行的想法是我们只记录整个消息。因此，我们不必用计算机的声音说“晚安，亲爱的，我爱你”，而是可以录制某人说的“晚安，亲爱的，我爱你”，用他们的声音，就像他们真正的语调和含义一样。

paras.en: Sanders: The beauty of these messages is that they capture the quirks of a person’s voice.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：这些信息的美妙之处在于它们捕捉到了一个人声音的怪癖。

paras.en: Nilson: You know, I live in Minnesota, and so there’s a lot of ooftas and doncha knows, and those kinds of things that do not come out right when you type them into a computer.
paras.zh: 尼尔森：你知道，我住在明尼苏达州，所以有很多 ooftas 和 doncha 知道的东西，当你把它们输入电脑时，这些东西不会正确显示。

paras.en: Sanders: Nilson encounters these sorts of sounds when she’s helping people save recordings of their voice for the future.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：尼尔森在帮助人们保存自己的声音录音以供将来使用时遇到了这类声音。

paras.en: Nilson: You gotta get all those right sayings with the right, you know, “o’s” in them.
paras.zh: 尼尔森：你必须让所有这些正确的说法都带有正确的“o”。

paras.en: Sanders: These recorded messages are often things like an inside joke with the exact right timing or a favorite little nickname for someone special.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：这些录制的信息通常是恰逢其时的内部笑话，或者是给某个特别的人最喜欢的小绰号。

paras.en: Nilson: It can be really emotional. And that’s, when you’re recording the sentences that are predetermined and they’re not sentences that you would normally say, that can be easy. But when your family has written down a list of meaningful words that they want to hear in your voice and you know that you’re recording it because you might lose your voice, that can be really emotional. And it can be hard. And I fully understand that, but we can also have fun with it.
paras.zh: 尼尔森：这可能真的很情绪化。也就是说，当您录制预先确定的句子并且它们不是您通常会说的句子时，这可能很容易。但是，当您的家人写下一系列他们希望在您的声音中听到的有意义的单词，并且您知道您录制它是因为您可能会失去声音时，这可能会非常情绪化。这可能很难。我完全理解这一点，但我们也可以从中获得乐趣。

paras.en: Sanders: Pre-recorded jokes come up pretty often when people are choosing what messages to preserve for later use. And swear words come up surprisingly often too, Nilson tells me.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：当人们选择保留哪些消息以供以后使用时，经常会出现预先录制的笑话。尼尔森告诉我，脏话也经常出现，令人惊讶。

paras.en: Nilson: I had someone come in just the other day, and they had an entire category of recorded cuss words. So that’s important. Well, right? I mean, you don’t want them to be monotone when you’re frustrated. You want the right emphasis to come out on that.
paras.zh: 尼尔森：前几天有人进来，他们录下了一大堆脏话。所以这很重要。嗯，对吧？我的意思是，当你感到沮丧时，你不希望它们变得单调。你希望对此有正确的强调。

paras.en: Sanders: It takes the sails out of it for sure if it’s monotone.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：如果它是单调的，那么它肯定会变得毫无意义。

paras.en: Nilson: Yeah, exactly. I mean, that’s communication, right? That’s important communication. So I guess it doesn’t really surprise me anymore, but it’s fun nonetheless.
paras.zh: 尼尔森：是的，完全正确。我的意思是，这就是沟通，对吗？这是重要的沟通。所以我想这不再让我感到惊讶，但仍然很有趣。

paras.en: Sanders: She says some people come to her with entire folders of swears, folders that she refused to share with me for the story, by the way.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：她说有些人带着一整套脏话来找她，顺便说一句，她拒绝与我分享这些文件夹。

paras.en: Nilson: The best part is it was a swear folder with all these different swear words and like different sayings and whatever. And then just one of them had a call-out to a specific person. And I was like, what did that person do to you that he’s the only one that has a specific? And then he laughed and he typed out, “If you knew him, you’d understand.”
paras.zh: 尼尔森：最好的部分是它是一个脏话文件夹，里面有所有这些不同的脏话，比如不同的谚语等等。然后其中只有一个人向特定的人发出了呼唤。我当时想，那个人对你做了什么，他是唯一一个有具体行动的人？然后他笑了，打字道：“如果你认识他，你就会明白。”

paras.en: Sanders: All of these quirks, the swears, the smiles in the voice, the familiar jokes, all of these things make a particular voice special. Jules created a banked voice. He didn’t love the result.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：所有这些怪癖、脏话、声音中的微笑、熟悉的笑话，所有这些都让特定的声音变得特别。朱尔斯发出了沉闷的声音。他不喜欢这个结果。

paras.en: Jules: What I learned from banking my voice was that it really wasn’t my voice. It was more like a robot trying to emulate my voice. It had no emotion or tone behind it.
paras.zh: 朱尔斯：我从储存我的声音中学到的是，这实际上不是我的声音。它更像是一个试图模仿我声音的机器人。它背后没有任何情感或语气。

paras.en: Sanders: This was a problem because it got in the way of something Jules wanted to do. The turmoil of ALS forced some clarity for him about what he wanted out of life, what he wanted to spend his time doing. And one of those answers, it turns out, was comedy. After his diagnosis, while he still had his voice, he performed stand-up a few times.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：这是一个问题，因为它妨碍了朱尔斯想做的事情。 ALS 的混乱迫使他清楚地认识到自己想要从生活中得到什么，想要把时间花在做什么上。事实证明，这些答案之一就是喜剧。确诊后，他在还能说话的情况下表演了几次单口相声。

paras.en: Sanders: But as his voice got harder to use, things changed. Jules could still talk, but it took a lot of work, especially since he was often using a mask for extra oxygen.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：但随着他的声音变得越来越难用，情况发生了变化。朱尔斯仍然可以说话，但这需要做很多工作，特别是因为他经常使用面罩获取额外的氧气。

paras.en: MA: He was wearing the mask pretty much the entire time. So his voice was very labored, because you have to take the breath in to utter anything. So it was very choppy. But he did have a voice.
paras.zh: MA：他几乎一直戴着面具。所以他的声音非常吃力，因为你必须屏住呼吸才能说出任何话。所以它非常不稳定。但他确实有声音。

paras.en: Sanders: With time, a live performance with his original voice became impossible. The next option was to use a banked voice, but that wasn’t good enough for a comedy performance.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：随着时间的推移，用他的原声进行现场表演变得不可能了。下一个选择是使用银行声音，但这对于喜剧表演来说还不够好。

paras.en: MA: So then he started to lose his voice and he was like, I don’t, you know, I can’t pull this off with a banked voice because it’s so robotic. It’s monotone. You can’t really do it.
paras.zh: MA：然后他开始失去声音，他说，我不知道，你知道，我无法用固定的声音来完成这个任务，因为它太机械了。很单调。你真的做不到。

paras.en: Sanders: Jules couldn’t pull off a comedy show. But could there be a different way, a different voice?
paras.zh: 桑德斯：朱尔斯无法完成喜剧表演。但能否有不同的方式、不同的声音呢？

paras.en: I’m going to step back here and give you more context about Jules and about ALS. ALS is progressive and relentless, which means over time, more and more of the motor neurons in the brain and spinal cord are affected, and symptoms get worse.
paras.zh: 我将回到这里，为您提供有关 Jules 和 ALS 的更多背景信息。 ALS 是进行性且持续的，这意味着随着时间的推移，大脑和脊髓中越来越多的运动神经元受到影响，症状会变得更糟。

paras.en: And though this progression varies quite a bit from person to person, the median survival time after an ALS diagnosis is about 30 months. Time is short here. This diagnosis forces big choices about how to live and what a person wants their remaining time to include, for them and for their family. In the middle of everything else going on, Jules was facing a choice that many people in his situation must confront, whether or not he would get a tracheostomy.
paras.zh: 尽管这种进展因人而异，但 ALS 诊断后的中位生存时间约为 30 个月。这里时间很短。这一诊断迫使人们做出重大选择，决定如何生活，以及一个人希望在剩下的时间里为自己和家人做什么。在所有其他事情发生的过程中，朱尔斯面临着许多与他处境相同的人必须面对的选择，无论他是否接受气管切开术。

paras.en: That’s a procedure in which doctors place a tube in the throat. This tube is then connected to a ventilator that breathes for a person.
paras.zh: 这是医生将一根管子插入喉咙的手术。然后将该管连接到为人呼吸的呼吸机。

paras.en: The procedure can leave a person unable to speak again, with whatever residual voice they might have left. Now, we have spent this episode on what it feels like to lose your voice. Jules was losing his. So it might seem like this part of the decision wouldn’t matter all that much. But to a person who’s losing their voice, and to their family, this moment marks an end point. It’s a hard stop.
paras.zh: 该手术可能会使一个人无法再说话，无论他们可能剩下什么声音。现在，我们用这一集来探讨失去声音的感觉。朱尔斯正在失去他的。因此，这部分决定似乎并不那么重要。但对于一个失声的人和他们的家人来说，这一刻标志着一个终点。这是一个艰难的停止。

paras.en: MA: He was someone who didn’t want to do a tracheostomy. He was opting for, once I’m done, that’s it. And that was our plan.
paras.zh: MA：他是一个不想做气管切开术的人。他选择的是，一旦我完成了，就这样了。这就是我们的计划。

paras.en: Sanders: As Jules and MA confront this decision, could a different sort of voice change the story?
paras.zh: 桑德斯：当朱尔斯和马萨诸塞州面临这个决定时，不同的声音可以改变这个故事吗？

paras.en: Jules: So when I first heard my cloned voice, it felt like I reappeared. When my wife first heard it, she cried because of how close it sounded like me before I lost my voice.
paras.zh: 朱尔斯：所以当我第一次听到我的克隆声音时，感觉就像我重新出现了一样。当我妻子第一次听到这首歌时，她哭了，因为这听起来太像我失声之前的我了。

paras.en: Sanders: This is The Deep End. Talk to me. I’m Laura Sanders. If you like this podcast, tell your friends and leave us a review. It helps the show a lot.
paras.zh: 桑德斯：这就是深渊。跟我说话。我是劳拉·桑德斯。如果您喜欢这个播客，请告诉您的朋友并给我们留下评论。对节目帮助很大。

paras.en: Send us your questions and your comments at podcasts@sciencenews.org. The Deep End is a production of Science News. It’s based on original reporting by me, Laura Sanders. This episode was produced and mixed by Ella Rowen. Our project manager is Ashley Yeager. Nancy Schute is our editor in chief. Our music is by Blue Dot Sessions. The podcast is made possible in part by the Burroughs Wellcome Fund with support from PRX.
paras.zh: 请通过 podcasts@sciencenews.org 将您的问题和意见发送给我们。 《The Deep End》是《科学新闻》的制作。它基于我劳拉·桑德斯的原创报道。本集由 Ella Rowen 制作和混音。我们的项目经理是阿什利·耶格尔。南希·舒特 (Nancy Schute) 是我们的主编。我们的音乐是由 Blue Dot Sessions 制作的。该播客的部分制作是由 Burroughs Wellcome 基金在 PRX 的支持下完成的。

paras.en: This podcast was produced with support from the Burroughs Wellcome Fund and in partnership with PRX. The podcast logo was created by Neil Webb.
paras.zh: 该播客是在 Burroughs Wellcome 基金的支持下并与 PRX 合作制作的。播客徽标由尼尔·韦伯创建。

articles.title: A duo goes against the tide to explain an origin of human endurance
articles.author: Elizabeth Pennisi

paras.en: Two researchers may have opened floodgates on the debate over why humans can run marathons, swim the English Channel or dive a hundred meters and back on a single breath and their ape cousins can’t.
paras.zh: 两位研究人员可能开启了关于为什么人类可以跑马拉松、游过英吉利海峡或一口气潜水一百米来回的争论，而他们的猿类表亲却不能。

paras.en: Humans evolved endurance for feats like these not just by running down prey on the African savanna, but also by diving for food in lakes or coastal waters, the duo propose September 17 in PaleoAnthropology. The hypothesis adds complexity to a decades-old theory that puts the drivers for evolution exclusively on land. But it coexists with a history of pushback for any water-related ideas.
paras.zh: 两人在 9 月 17 日的《古人类学》杂志上提出，人类不仅通过在非洲大草原上追捕猎物，还通过在湖泊或沿海水域潜水寻找食物来进化出这样的耐力。这一假说使已有数十年历史的理论变得更加复杂，该理论将进化的驱动力完全集中在陆地上。但它与任何与水有关的想法都受到抵制的历史并存。

paras.en: The work is causing ripples among anthropologists. “I could not work out [at first] if this was groundbreaking or dumb,” says Christian Tryon, a paleoanthropologist at the University of Connecticut in Storrs.
paras.zh: 这项工作在人类学家中引起了轩然大波。 “一开始我无法弄清楚这是开创性的还是愚蠢的，”康涅狄格大学斯托斯分校的古人类学家克里斯蒂安·特赖恩 (Christian Tryon) 说。

paras.en: In 1960, researchers came up with what’s been called the aquatic ape or waterside hypothesis, which suggested that our ancestors evolved longer legs and other adaptations from swimming for their suppers in watery habitats. Popularized in media accounts but not adequately vetted in peer-reviewed journals, the idea was shunned by the scientific community as additional fossils pointed away from a life in water. More recently, the dominant theory has been that it was landlocked human ancestors who gradually developed our remarkable endurance. “There’s been this reluctance to really think about anything sort of water-related as important in human evolution,” Tryon says.
paras.zh: 1960 年，研究人员提出了所谓的水生猿或水边假说，该假说表明，我们的祖先通过在水生栖息地游泳以获取晚餐而进化出更长的腿和其他适应能力。这一想法在媒体报道中广为流传，但在同行评审期刊中并未得到充分审查，但由于更多的化石表明不存在水中生命，科学界回避了这一想法。最近，主流理论认为，正是内陆人类祖先逐渐发展出了我们非凡的耐力。特赖恩说：“人们一直不愿意真正考虑与水有关的任何事情在人类进化中的重要性。”

paras.en: Yet evolutionary anthropologist Josephine Joordens, a self-professed “water person” who trained as a marine biologist, had long wondered whether coastal life was vital to the evolutionary process, because it provides easy access to both water and land resources. Joordens combined forces with Erika Schagatay, a physiologist at Mid-Sweden University in Östersund, to formulate what they call the “dive first, run later” hypothesis.
paras.zh: 然而，进化人类学家约瑟芬·乔登斯（Josephine Joordens）自称是“水人”，接受过海洋生物学家培训，她长期以来一直想知道沿海生物是否对进化过程至关重要，因为它可以轻松获取水和土地资源。乔登斯与厄斯特松德中瑞典大学生理学家埃里卡·沙加泰 (Erika Schagatay) 合作，提出了他们所谓的“先潜水，后跑步”的假设。

paras.en: Schagatay — herself a freediver — has spent decades observing and monitoring modern sea foraging people such as the Ama in Japan and the Sama-Bajau in Southeast Asia. Joordens studied fossil evidence and combed the literature about aquatic activities. Our evolution “was likely a very complex and very dynamic process,” says Joordens, of the Max Planck Institute for Evolutionary Anthropology in Leipzig, Germany.
paras.zh: 沙加泰本人是一名自由潜水员，她花了数十年的时间观察和监测现代海上觅食人类，例如日本的海女和东南亚的萨玛巴瑶人。乔登斯研究了化石证据并梳理了有关水生活动的文献。德国莱比锡马克斯普朗克进化人类学研究所的乔登斯说，我们的进化“可能是一个非常复杂和动态的过程”。

paras.en: They propose some Homo species wound up shallow-water diving repeatedly about 2 million to 3 million years ago, much the way the Sama-Bajau do today. These people spend four to six hours per day repeatedly diving several meters deep to catch fish and collect shellfish and other food. They evolved bigger spleens than their non-diving counterparts and, it seems, enhanced respiratory and cardiovascular capacity. They have the ability to “pace” breathing periods and breath-holding to avoid fatigue. In our ancestors, that could have paved the way for the cardiorespiratory stamina needed in modern endurance running, Schagatay says.
paras.zh: 他们提出，一些人种在大约 200 万到 300 万年前就反复进行浅水潜水，就像今天的萨玛巴瑶人那样。这些人每天花四到六个小时反复潜入几米深的地方捕鱼、收集贝类和其他食物。他们进化出比非潜水同伴更大的脾脏，并且呼吸和心血管能力似乎得到增强。他们能够“调整”呼吸周期和屏气以避免疲劳。沙加泰说，对于我们的祖先来说，这可能为现代耐力跑所需的心肺耐力铺平了道路。

paras.en: These Homo divers evolved heavy bones to help stay underwater and downward facing noses to keep water out, the two suggest. They eventually passed those endurance-boosting traits on to other populations with lighter bones and a more terrestrial lifestyle.
paras.zh: 两人表示，这些人种潜水员进化出了沉重的骨骼来帮助留在水下，并进化出向下的鼻子来防水。他们最终将这些增强耐力的特征传递给了其他骨骼更轻、生活方式更陆地的人群。

paras.en: The study “shows there is a lot of evidence” for forage diving as an early evolutionary driver, says Leslea Hlusko, a paleobiologist at the Centro Nacional de Investigación sobre la Evolución Humana in Burgos, Spain.
paras.zh: 西班牙布尔戈斯国家人类进化研究中心的古生物学家 Leslea Hlusko 表示，这项研究“有大量证据”表明，觅食潜水是早期进化的驱动力。

paras.en: This idea is not a retread of the aquatic ape theory, says Christopher Ruff, a biological anthropologist at Johns Hopkins School of Medicine. “Occasional aquatic foraging is quite a different proposal“ from the discredited theory’s primarily aquatic existence and should be taken seriously, Ruff says.
paras.zh: 约翰·霍普金斯大学医学院的生物人类学家克里斯托弗·拉夫说，这个想法并不是对水生猿理论的翻版。拉夫说，“偶尔的水生觅食是一个完全不同的提议”，与这种不可信的主要水生存在的理论截然不同，应该认真对待。

paras.en: Not everyone thinks the dive first idea holds water.
paras.zh: 并非所有人都认为“潜水第一”的想法站得住脚。

paras.en: Multiple factors work against the idea that diving could have helped humans become better endurance runners, says Daniel Lieberman, a paleoanthropologist at Harvard University. He argues that endurance diving does not require an enhanced aerobic capacity: It slows the heart rate, whereas running speeds it up. He disputes how and why heavy bones arose; they could have developed in people who used their bodies for heavy work and not because such bones helped divers with buoyancy issues. Nor is the downward pointed nose meaningful given that many diving mammals have forward facing noses. Other reasons, such as keeping the air in nostrils moist, were probably more important in selecting for this feature, he says.
paras.zh: 哈佛大学古人类学家丹尼尔·利伯曼 (Daniel Lieberman) 表示，多种因素不利于潜水可以帮助人类成为更好的耐力跑者的观点。他认为耐力潜水不需要增强有氧能力：它会减慢心率，而跑步会加快心率。他对重骨头如何以及为何产生提出了争议。它们可能是在那些用身体从事繁重工作的人身上形成的，而不是因为这些骨头可以帮助潜水员解决浮力问题。考虑到许多潜水哺乳动物的鼻子都朝前，向下尖的鼻子也没有意义。他说，其他原因，例如保持鼻孔内的空气湿润，可能在选择此功能时更重要。

paras.en: What’s more, many people around the world have long relied on running down game for food, says archaeologist Eugène Morin of Trent University in Peterborough, Canada. “Diving is costly and the [caloric] returns are low,” so early humans would not choose to dive if other foraging opportunities existed, he argues.
paras.zh: 加拿大彼得伯勒特伦特大学的考古学家尤金·莫林表示，更重要的是，世界各地的许多人长期以来一直依靠捕猎野味来获取食物。他认为，“潜水成本高昂，而且[热量]回报很低”，因此如果存在其他觅食机会，早期人类不会选择潜水。

paras.en: Critiques aside, “the simple ‘ape walked out from forest to savanna’ story clearly does not cut it anymore,” says Pascal Gagneux, a biological anthropologist at the University of California, San Diego. Coastal routes around Africa, along Africa’s lakeshores and out of Africa “must have played a huge role” in human evolution, Gagneux says.
paras.zh: 抛开批评不谈，“简单的‘猿从森林走到稀树草原’的故事显然已经不再适用了，”加州大学圣地亚哥分校的生物人类学家帕斯卡·加格纽克斯(Pascal Gagneux)说。加格纽克斯说，围绕非洲、沿着非洲湖岸以及走出非洲的沿海路线在人类进化中“一定发挥了巨大作用”。

paras.en: The pair knows they risk the ire of their peers in presenting this “dive first” hypothesis, but Joordens says, “we are both in our early 60s and we both have beautiful careers, so we thought ‘whatever happens, happens.’”
paras.zh: 两人知道提出这种“潜水优先”的假设可能会激怒同侪，但乔登斯说，“我们都 60 岁出头，而且都拥有美好的职业生涯，所以我们认为‘无论发生什么，都会发生。’”

paras.en: And Tryon ultimately found the paper worth the read. “If nothing else, it gets people thinking and it gets people looking.”
paras.zh: 特赖恩最终发现这篇论文值得一读。 “如果不出意外的话，它会让人们思考，让人们寻找。”

articles.title: To turn invisible, we need to tweak the path light travels
articles.author: Sofia Caetano Avritzer

paras.en: It’s pretty hard to fight an opponent you can’t see. That’s what makes Invisible Woman an invaluable member of the Fantastic Four. She can disappear in the blink of an eye and take out entire factions of enemies, all while her adversaries kick and punch empty air.
paras.zh: 与看不见的对手战斗是非常困难的。这就是隐形女侠成为神奇四侠中无价的成员的原因。她可以在眨眼之间消失并消灭整个敌人派系，而她的对手却在空中拳打脚踢。

paras.en: Characters with invisibility powers — Marvel Comics’ Invisible Woman (aka Sue Storm), H.G. Wells’ Invisible Man and The Incredibles’ Violet Parr — can do all sorts of cool things. Escape embarrassing situations. Snoop on other people. Go places where they’re not allowed.
paras.zh: 拥有隐形能力的角色——漫威漫画的隐形女侠（又名苏·斯托姆）、H.G.威尔斯的隐形人和超人总动员的维奥莱特·帕尔——可以做各种很酷的事情。逃离尴尬的境地。窥探其他人。去他们不允许去的地方。

paras.en: Short of a theoretical invisibility cloak, that kind of lurking is impossible for us. But some animals can hide in plain sight by turning nearly transparent.
paras.zh: 如果没有理论上的隐形斗篷，这种潜伏对我们来说是不可能的。但有些动物可以通过变得近乎透明来隐藏在众目睽睽之下。

paras.en: Invisibility is useful for animals that spend a lot of time in places with no good hiding spots, such as the air or open ocean, says Kate Feller, a visual ecologist at Union College in Schenectady, N.Y.
paras.zh: 纽约州斯克内克塔迪联合学院的视觉生态学家凯特·费勒表示，对于那些长时间待在空气或公海等没有良好藏身之处的动物来说，隐形非常有用。

paras.en: The secret to invisibility is all about light. “The way we see things is when light is reflected back off of an object onto our eyes,” Feller says. The more light that can pass through something undisturbed, the harder it is to see that thing.
paras.zh: 隐形的秘密就在于光。 “我们看到事物的方式是光线从物体反射回我们的眼睛，”费勒说。能穿过不受干扰的物体的光线越多，看到该物体就越困难。

paras.en: Light can’t easily pass through most animals, but those with nearly invisible body parts have tricks to get around this hurdle.
paras.zh: 光无法轻易穿过大多数动物，但那些身体部位几乎看不见的动物却有办法绕过这个障碍。

paras.en: Animals get their colors from pigments, compounds that appear as different colors depending on which wavelengths of light they absorb and which they reflect. Green pigments, for instance, reflect green light and absorb all other colors. Invisibility requires getting rid of these colorful compounds.
paras.zh: 动物从颜料和化合物中获得颜色，这些化合物根据它们吸收和反射的光波长而呈现不同的颜色。例如，绿色颜料反射绿光并吸收所有其他颜色。隐形需要摆脱这些彩色化合物。

paras.en: Most baby fish lack pigments at first, helping them hide from predators. Some species stay see-through their whole lives. One is the ghost catfish (Kryptopterus vitreolus). With a body that’s fully transparent from gills to tail, it looks like a floating head from afar.
paras.zh: 大多数幼鱼一开始都缺乏色素，这有助于它们躲避捕食者。有些物种一生都保持透明。其中一种是幽灵鲶鱼（Kryptopterus vitreolus）。它的身体从鳃到尾巴都是完全透明的，远远望去就像一个漂浮的头。

paras.en: It’s hard to hide every body part, though. Eyes need light-absorbing pigments to see. And even clear stomachs will show up if animals eat colorful food. A ghost catfish eats only small bits of food and its long, thin, tubelike stomach stretches out a meal, helping the organ stay hidden, says Qibin Zhao, a physicist and materials scientist at Shanghai Jiao Tong University in China. Blood can’t be transparent either due to the iron-rich hemoglobin molecules that carry oxygen. So up close, the ghost catfish’s blood vessels are still visible.
paras.zh: 不过，很难隐藏身体的每一个部位。眼睛需要吸收光的色素才能看到东西。如果动物吃彩色食物，甚至会出现清澈的胃。中国上海交通大学的物理学家兼材料科学家赵其斌说，幽灵鲶鱼只吃少量食物，它又长又薄的管状胃可以伸出食物，帮助该器官隐藏起来。由于富含铁的血红蛋白分子携带氧气，血液也不透明。所以近距离观察，鬼鲶鱼的血管依然清晰可见。

paras.en: But even pigment-free objects are not entirely invisible. Light travels at different speeds through different materials so will bend or bounce when it goes from one material to another. That can create a shine, like sun reflecting off a puddle.
paras.zh: 但即使是无色素的物体也不是完全看不见的。光以不同的速度穿过不同的材料，因此当它从一种材料传播到另一种材料时会弯曲或反弹。这可以产生光泽，就像阳光从水坑反射一样。

paras.en: That’s not a big problem for a glasswing butterfly (Greta oto): Its wings have fewer reflective scales than other butterflies’ wings. The wings are also covered in tiny wax bumps that make light’s transition from air to tissue more gradual, so light passes through the wings mostly undisturbed.
paras.zh: 对于玻璃翅蝴蝶（Greta oto）来说，这不是一个大问题：它的翅膀比其他蝴蝶的翅膀具有更少的反光鳞片。翅膀上还覆盖着微小的蜡块，使光线从空气到组织的过渡更加平缓，因此光线穿过翅膀时基本上不受干扰。

paras.en: Invisible Woman uses a completely different vanishing trick than real-life transparent animals. Instead of letting light pass through her, she bends lights rays to completely avoid her body. The rays never even touch her, so they are not reflected or absorbed, making her invisible to any onlookers.
paras.zh: 隐形女侠使用了与现实生活中的透明动物完全不同的消失技巧。她没有让光线穿过她，而是弯曲光线以完全避开她的身体。光线甚至从未接触过她，因此不会被反射或吸收，使任何旁观者都看不到她。

paras.en: In 2006, scientists proposed that this same logic could be used to create an invisibility cloak. But in practice, a material that perfectly bends light rays is expensive, hard to make and can divert only a narrow band of light at a time. That’s just enough to make a single-colored object disappear but not an entire human.
paras.zh: 2006年，科学家提出同样的逻辑可以用来制造隐形斗篷。但在实践中，能够完美弯曲光线的材料价格昂贵，难以制造，并且一次只能转移很窄的光带。这足以使一个单色物体消失，但不足以使整个人消失。

paras.en: And there’s another problem: With no light getting into the cloak, a person inside can’t see out. Luckily, Sue Storm has the ability to use cosmic rays to see while she’s invisible, allowing her to protect the world from supervillains like Doctor Doom.
paras.zh: 还有另一个问题：斗篷里没有光线，里面的人看不到外面。幸运的是，苏·斯托姆有能力利用宇宙射线在隐形状态下看到东西，这让她能够保护世界免受末日博士等超级恶棍的侵害。

articles.title: Thousands of Handwritten Records Recovered From Archives Reveal The True Scale of Warming in The Congo
articles.author: Jess Cockerill

paras.en: For wealthy and politically stable nations, the task of maintaining and digitizing climate records is a high-tech enterprise.
paras.zh: 对于富裕和政治稳定的国家来说，维护和数字化气候记录的任务是一项高科技事业。

paras.en: But this has not been the case in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).
paras.zh: 但刚果民主共和国（DRC）的情况并非如此。

paras.en: Much of the Congo Basin's climate data for the past century has been recorded on paper, written by hand, and stored in an archive in a town called Yangambi.
paras.zh: 刚果盆地上个世纪的大部分气候数据都是手写在纸上记录的，并存储在一个名叫扬比姆的小镇的档案馆中。

paras.en: Now, a scientist on a mission to digitize Central Africa's climate archives has revealed the scale of climate warming in the Congo, in collaboration with researchers from the DRC and Belgium.
paras.zh: 现在，一位致力于将中非气候档案数字化的科学家与刚果民主共和国和比利时的研究人员合作，揭示了刚果气候变暖的规模。

paras.en: The results are published in Earth System Dynamics.
paras.zh: 研究结果发表在《地球系统动力学》上。

paras.en: Hydrologist Derrick Muheki is originally from south-west Uganda, near the eastern border of the DRC, but to pursue his PhD he traveled to Belgium's Vrije Universiteit Brussel.
paras.zh: 水文学家 Derrick Muheki 来自乌干达西南部，靠近刚果民主共和国东部边境，但为了攻读博士学位，他前往比利时布鲁塞尔自由大学。

paras.en: In Belgium, Muheki had easy access to colonial-era documents detailing the Congo's climate through the early 20th century. But those records end after the 1950s.
paras.zh: 在比利时，Muheki 可以轻松获得殖民时代的文件，详细介绍了 20 世纪初刚果的气候。但这些记录在 20 世纪 50 年代之后就结束了。

paras.en: Belgium occupied the Congo as a colony from 1908 until 1960, when Congolese leaders obtained independence for the country we now know as the DRC.
paras.zh: 1908 年至 1960 年，比利时占领刚果作为殖民地，1960 年刚果领导人为我们现在称为刚果民主共和国的国家获得独立。

paras.en: In Belgium, "meteorological logs are stored in metal boxes and acid-free paper under controlled temperature and humidity," he explained.
paras.zh: 在比利时，“气象日志在受控的温度和湿度下储存在金属盒和无酸纸中，”他解释道。

paras.en: "In Yangambi, those resources simply aren't available."
paras.zh: “在扬比姆，根本无法获得这些资源。”

paras.en: The records in Yangambi are thorough and detailed: they just hadn't been digitized or published in a way international climate researchers could access.
paras.zh: 扬比姆的记录详尽而详尽：它们只是没有以国际气候研究人员可以访问的方式数字化或出版。

paras.en: "The persistent data sparsity across Central Africa has been a significant impediment to studies assessing the regional effects of human-induced climate change on ecosystems, societies, and the water cycle, despite the region hosting the Congo Basin, which contains the world's second-largest river and tropical rainforest," Muheki and team write in their new paper.
paras.zh: Muheki 和团队在他们的新论文中写道：“尽管刚果盆地所在的地区拥有世界第二大河流和热带雨林，但中部非洲地区持续的数据稀疏一直是评估人为气候变化对生态系统、社会和水循环的区域影响的研究的重大障碍。”

paras.en: It's not easy to get to Yangambi. The roads connecting this town to its neighbors are unpaved and, according to Wikipedia, "difficult to use at all times of the year".
paras.zh: 去仰安比并不容易。连接这个城镇和邻居的道路尚未铺砌，根据维基百科的说法，“一年中的任何时候都难以使用”。

paras.en: "The motorbike is the main mode of public transport there," Muheki said.
paras.zh: “摩托车是那里的主要公共交通方式，”穆赫基说。

paras.en: "I sat on the back while my equipment – a camera, lamps and a generous supply of batteries – traveled on a second bike. There's no electricity grid in the area, not even in the archive itself. The only power comes from batteries and generators."
paras.zh: “我坐在后面，而我的设备——相机、灯和充足的电池——则骑在第二辆自行车上行驶。该地区没有电网，甚至档案馆本身也没有。唯一的电力来自电池和发电机。”

paras.en: You might wonder why the DRC's meteorological records are kept in such a remote place.
paras.zh: 您可能想知道为什么刚果民主共和国的气象记录保存在如此偏远的地方。

paras.en: In the Belgian Congo, plantations were a major part of the colony's economic policy. Yangambi became a hub for agriculture and forestry research to serve that aim, with a dedicated center built right on the banks of the Congo River.
paras.zh: 在比属刚果，种植园是该殖民地经济政策的重要组成部分。为了实现这一目标，扬比姆成为了农业和林业研究中心，并在刚果河沿岸建立了一个专门的中心。

paras.en: When the country gained independence, the research center at Yangambi was renamed the National Institute of Agronomic Studies and Research (INERA), which still operates today.
paras.zh: 该国获得独立后，扬比比的研究中心更名为国家农艺研究所 (INERA)，至今仍在运作。

paras.en: And it was at INERA's Section de Climatologie that Muheki got to work digitizing more than 9,000 handwritten pages of daily meteorological records, collected from 37 weather stations across the country.
paras.zh: 正是在 INERA 的气候科，Muheki 开始对从全国 37 个气象站收集的 9,000 多页手写每日气象记录进行数字化。

paras.en: "Documents were stacked on open shelves, exposed to moisture and insects," he described.
paras.zh: “文件堆放在开放的架子上，暴露在潮湿和昆虫的环境中，”他描述道。

paras.en: "Just a few months before I arrived, there had even been a fire in another wing of the building. Seeing that really drives home how fragile paper archives are – and how urgent it is to save this data before it disappears."
paras.zh: “就在我到达之前的几个月，大楼的另一翼甚至发生了火灾。看到这一点确实让人们明白纸质档案是多么脆弱——以及在这些数据消失之前保存这些数据是多么紧迫。”

paras.en: Muheki and his colleagues have now pieced together a continuous digital record of the Congo Basin's climate from 1908 to 2023, transcribing the handwritten records from Yangambi with a machine learning tool called MeteoSaver, which Muheki helped develop.
paras.zh: Muheki 和他的同事现在已经拼凑出了 1908 年至 2023 年刚果盆地气候的连续数字记录，并使用 Muheki 帮助开发的名为 MeteoSaver 的机器学习工具转录了 Yangambi 的手写记录。

paras.en: The data reveals the Congo Basin climate has been changing in ways consistent with trends seen across the world: hot days are getting hotter and more frequent, while cold days are dwindling.
paras.zh: 数据显示，刚果盆地气候的变化与世界各地的趋势一致：炎热的天气越来越热、越来越频繁，而寒冷的天气正在减少。

paras.en: During the period with the best station coverage (1961–1990), days with hot extremes were almost twice as frequent in the most recent decade (the 1980s) as they were in the earliest (the 1960s).
paras.zh: 在气象站覆盖范围最好的时期（1961年至1990年），最近十年（20世纪80年代）极端炎热天气的发生频率几乎是最早（1960年代）的两倍。

paras.en: Between 1961 and 1990, average temperatures in the DRC rose by 0.5°C, and maximums increased by about 0.7°C. Those warming trends have continued into the 21st century.
paras.zh: 1961 年至 1990 年间，刚果民主共和国的平均气温上升了 0.5°C，最高气温上升了约 0.7°C。这些变暖趋势一直持续到21世纪。

paras.en: "These findings provide new observational evidence of climate change in this data-sparse region and underline the critical need for more climate data rescue efforts to improve assessments of observed changes in climate," Muheki and his colleagues write.
paras.zh: Muheki 和他的同事写道：“这些发现为这个数据稀疏地区的气候变化提供了新的观测证据，并强调迫切需要更多的气候数据救援工作，以改进对观测到的气候变化的评估。”

paras.en: "Accessing more of these records will help us improve reconstructions of our climate history or improve our projections of future climate change in this part of the world, where adaptation to climate impacts is already a necessity," Muheki says.
paras.zh: 穆赫基说：“获取更多这些记录将有助于我们改善气候历史的重建，或改善我们对世界这一地区未来气候变化的预测，在这些地区，适应气候影响已经是必要的。”

paras.en: The research has been published in Earth System Dynamics.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《地球系统动力学》上。

articles.title: A New Injection Makes Fat Cells Self-Destruct, And Might Prevent GLP-1 Weight Regain
articles.author: David Nield

paras.en: Early clinical trials into a new fat reduction treatment have reported promising results, and the treatment takes a more unusual approach: Rather than shrinking fat cells, as most weight loss strategies do, it safely and naturally kills them off.
paras.zh: 一种新的减脂疗法的早期临床试验已经报告了有希望的结果，并且该疗法采用了一种更不寻常的方法：它不像大多数减肥策略那样缩小脂肪细胞，而是安全、自然地杀死它们。

paras.en: The drug here is CBL-514, which is administered via injection. As well as proving effective at reducing subcutaneous fat (just below the skin), there's evidence it can also reduce visceral fat (stored deeper around the organs).
paras.zh: 这里的药物是 CBL-514，通过注射给药。除了被证明可以有效减少皮下脂肪（位于皮肤下方）之外，有证据表明它还可以减少内脏脂肪（储存在器官周围较深处）。

paras.en: According to the team behind the trials, CBL-514 and its unconventional strategy have the potential to reduce fat in key areas of the body – with further benefits that come with weight loss likely to follow.
paras.zh: 据试验背后的团队称，CBL-514 及其非常规策略有可能减少身体关键部位的脂肪，并可能随之带来减肥带来的进一步好处。

paras.en: "We expect that patients will be pleased by the cosmetic effects, such as the flatter stomach that can come with subcutaneous fat loss," says endocrinologist Timothy Garvey, from the University of Alabama at Birmingham, who headed up the trial.
paras.zh: 负责这项试验的阿拉巴马大学伯明翰分校内分泌学家蒂莫西·加维 (Timothy Garvey) 表示：“我们预计患者会对美容效果感到满意，例如减少皮下脂肪带来的平坦腹部。”

paras.en: "But it is the reduction in body weight, loss of visceral fat and the improvements in blood pressure, cholesterol and the like that should be associated with this that will be important for health."
paras.zh: “但与此相关的是体重的减轻、内脏脂肪的减少以及血压、胆固醇等的改善，这对健康很重要。”

paras.en: To be clear, these results haven't been peer-reviewed yet – they're from a conference presentation and company announcements, not a published study, so they should be taken with a grain of salt for now.
paras.zh: 需要明确的是，这些结果尚未经过同行评审——它们来自会议演示和公司公告，而不是已发表的研究，所以现在应该对它们持保留态度。

paras.en: There are several different components to the research. Two phase 2 clinical trials, CBL-0204 and CBL-0205, involved 107 and 173 participants respectively, and showed that CBL-514 was effective at reducing subcutaneous fat in the majority of the volunteers.
paras.zh: 该研究有几个不同的组成部分。两项 2 期临床试验 CBL-0204 和 CBL-0205 分别涉及 107 名和 173 名参与者，结果表明 CBL-514 可有效减少大多数志愿者的皮下脂肪。

paras.en: Since those trials were carried out, the records of a subset of 41 participants have been analyzed for changes in visceral fat too.
paras.zh: 自这些试验进行以来，我们还对 41 名参与者的记录进行了内脏脂肪变化的分析。

paras.en: Those given CBL-514 injections for up to 12 weeks showed an average reduction of 12.01 percent in visceral fat, while those on a placebo treatment averaged a visceral fat increase of 5.68 percent four weeks after their final injection.
paras.zh: 接受 CBL-514 注射长达 12 周的受试者的内脏脂肪平均减少了 12.01%，而接受安慰剂治疗的受试者在最后一次注射后 4 周内脏脂肪平均增加了 5.68%。

paras.en: "These results provide encouraging early evidence that CBL-514 can reduce visceral-fat volume in the abdominal region," says epidemiologist Marie Spreckley, from the University of Cambridge in the UK, who wasn't involved in the research.
paras.zh: “这些结果提供了令人鼓舞的早期证据，表明 CBL-514 可以减少腹部区域的内脏脂肪体积，”英国剑桥大学的流行病学家 Marie Spreckley 说，她没有参与这项研究。

paras.en: "Larger trials with longer follow-up will be important to establish whether the fat reduction lasts and whether it leads to improvements in health."
paras.zh: “更大规模的试验和更长时间的随访对于确定减脂是否持续以及是否会改善健康非常重要。”

paras.en: The final part of the picture so far comes from animal tests. Rats treated with the GLP-1 drug tirzepatide and CBL-514 together lost more weight on average than rats who were given doses of tirzepatide on its own.
paras.zh: 到目前为止，图片的最后一部分来自动物测试。使用 GLP-1 药物替泽帕肽和 CBL-514 一起治疗的大鼠比单独服用替泽帕肽的大鼠平均体重减轻更多。

paras.en: What's more, the rats given both medications gained less weight when the tirzepatide treatment was stopped.
paras.zh: 更重要的是，当停止替西帕肽治疗时，接受这两种药物治疗的老鼠体重增加较少。

paras.en: GLP-1 drugs like tirzepatide are commonly prescribed for type 2 diabetes and weight loss, and are named after the glucagon-like peptide-1 they're designed to mimic. While they can be very effective, any lost weight often returns after a GLP-1 course has finished.
paras.zh: GLP-1 药物（如替泽帕肽）通常用于治疗 2 型糖尿病和减肥，并以它们模仿的胰高血糖素样肽-1 命名。虽然它们非常有效，但 GLP-1 课程结束后，减掉的体重往往又会反弹。

paras.en: It's possible that the way CBL-514 causes fat cells to self-destruct (technically known as apoptosis) means it's then more difficult for the pounds to pile back on – but this part of the research needs to be investigated further in tests on people, while other effects of the treatment are also assessed.
paras.zh: CBL-514 导致脂肪细胞自毁（技术上称为细胞凋亡）的方式可能意味着体重更难增加——但这部分研究需要在人体测试中进一步研究，同时也评估治疗的其他效果。

paras.en: "To be a useful obesity therapy it will be critical to show that this doesn't increase the risk of fat accumulation in other organs or poorer control of blood fat and sugar levels," says metabolism researcher Justin Rochford, from the University of Aberdeen in the UK, who wasn't involved in the research.
paras.zh: 英国阿伯丁大学代谢研究员贾斯汀·罗奇福德（Justin Rochford）没有参与这项研究，他说：“要成为一种有用的肥胖疗法，关键是要证明这不会增加其他器官脂肪堆积的风险，也不会导致血脂和血糖水平控制不佳。”

paras.en: The researchers are now working towards larger trials with bigger groups of participants tracked over a longer time period, which will assess how the losses in fat might impact overall health.
paras.zh: 研究人员现在正致力于进行更大规模的试验，在更长的时间内跟踪更多的参与者群体，这将评估脂肪的减少如何影响整体健康。

paras.en: CBL-514 was originally developed to remove fatty lumps under the skin called lipomas, and so far, the signs are promising that the drug's targeted fat cell removal technique could be valuable much more broadly.
paras.zh: CBL-514 最初开发用于去除皮下称为脂肪瘤的脂肪块，到目前为止，有迹象表明该药物的靶向脂肪细胞去除技术可能具有更广泛的价值。

paras.en: "This is a highly innovative approach to obesity pharmacotherapy that has produced some remarkable results in early human trials," says Garvey.
paras.zh: 加维说：“这是一种高度创新的肥胖药物治疗方法，在早期人体试验中取得了一些显着的成果。”

articles.title: Earth's Core Is Leaking All Sorts of Materials That Have Been Trapped Since Our Planet's Birth
articles.author: Ivan Farkas

paras.en: Our early Earth was a heavy metal album cover: a molten ball covered in a global lava ocean, spewing lethal gases while being pelted by the flaming space-rocks of our Solar System's violently chaotic afterbirth.
paras.zh: 我们早期的地球是一张重金属专辑封面：一个覆盖在全球熔岩海洋中的熔球，喷出致命的气体，同时受到太阳系剧烈混乱的胞衣中燃烧的太空岩石的撞击。

paras.en: Over the next 4.5 billion years of hectic cosmo-geological time, it has settled down a bit, allowing humans, lemurs, and others to emerge.
paras.zh: 在接下来的 45 亿年忙碌的宇宙地质时间里，它已经稳定下来，让人类、狐猴和其他动物得以出现。

paras.en: A vision of this hellish ancient reality remains, (hopefully) never to be glimpsed by human eyes: our molten metallic core, blazing about as hotly as the surface of the Sun.
paras.zh: 这个地狱般的古老现实的景象仍然存在，（希望）人类的眼睛永远不会瞥见：我们熔化的金属核心，像太阳表面一样炽热。

paras.en: But our core constantly sends chemical messengers up through its layers, including the space-borne ingredients of its birth, locked away for about one-third the lifetime of the Universe.
paras.zh: 但我们的核心不断地通过它的各层向上发送化学信使，其中包括其诞生时的太空传播成分，这些化学信使被锁定了大约宇宙寿命的三分之一。

paras.en: This includes the hydrogen that was drawn in from the giant cloud of gas and dust that formed the Sun, which continues to ooze up from the core and turns into water in the mantle and crust – not a splashy-sloshy water, but a water trapped in minerals.
paras.zh: 这包括从形成太阳的巨大气体和尘埃云中吸收的氢，这些氢继续从核心渗出，并在地幔和地壳中变成水——不是溅起的水，而是被困在矿物质中的水。

paras.en: Accordingly, a team of geoscientists from the University of Science and Technology of China, in Hefei, wanted to determine a scientifically popular, age-old (technically Earth-old) question:
paras.zh: 因此，来自合肥中国科学技术大学的地球科学家团队想要确定一个科学上流行的、古老的（技术上是地球古老的）问题：

paras.en: Are the chemical differences in the deep mantle relics of our planet's crystallization from a magma ball, or evidence that the core and mantle have exchanged chemicals since time immemorial?
paras.zh: 地幔深处的化学差异是地球岩浆球结晶的遗迹，还是地核和地幔自远古以来就交换化学物质的证据？

paras.en: In a study published in Science Advances, the researchers used machine-learning-boosted "path-integral simulations" to explore the quantum action of molecules and atoms.
paras.zh: 在《科学进展》上发表的一项研究中，研究人员使用机器学习增强的“路径积分模拟”来探索分子和原子的量子作用。

paras.en: Are the chemical differences in the deep mantle relics of our planet's crystallization from a magma ball, or evidence that the core and mantle have exchanged chemicals since time immemorial?
paras.zh: 地幔深处的化学差异是地球岩浆球结晶的遗迹，还是地核和地幔自远古以来就交换化学物质的证据？

paras.en: Importantly, this allowed them to analyze the inner-Earth transport of hydrogen, which is an especially quantum-quirky atom due to its lightness.
paras.zh: 重要的是，这使他们能够分析氢在地球内部的传输，氢是一种特别量子奇特的原子，因为它很轻。

paras.en: They thus checked the ratio of deuterium to hydrogen, which measures the proportion of a heavier hydrogen isotope called deuterium to the regular ol' hydrogen, to see whether the lighter hydrogen was leaking upward through molten plumes erupting on the surface.
paras.zh: 因此，他们检查了氘与氢的比率，该比率测量了一种称为氘的较重氢同位素与普通氢的比例，以查看较轻的氢是否通过表面喷发的熔羽向上泄漏。

paras.en: The crystallization model, however, demonstrates that mineral-melt fractionation is pretty weak, so it would produce an even D/H distribution in the ancient mantle.
paras.zh: 然而，结晶模型表明矿物熔体分馏相当弱，因此它会在古代地幔中产生均匀的 D/H 分布。

paras.en: "Collectively, these results indicate that magma ocean crystallization yields a primitive mantle with an essentially homogeneous hydrogen isotope composition, despite large variations in pressure, temperature, and model assumptions," the researchers found.
paras.zh: 研究人员发现：“总的来说，这些结果表明，尽管压力、温度和模型假设存在很大差异，但岩浆海洋结晶产生了具有基本均匀氢同位素组成的原始地幔。”

paras.en: They found that the most important factor was the magma ocean's starting hydrogen isotope composition – other variables, including the initial water content (estimated at up to two ocean masses), had little influence on the result.
paras.zh: 他们发现最重要的因素是岩浆海洋的起始氢同位素组成——其他变量，包括初始水含量（估计最多为两个海洋质量），对结果影响不大。

paras.en: The reason is literally chaos, because the conditions were too violently energetic for deuterium and hydrogen to be neatly sorted through Earth's layers.
paras.zh: 原因实际上是混乱，因为氘和氢的能量过于剧烈，无法在地球各层中整齐地分类。

paras.en: For comparison, it's much easier to assemble a jigsaw puzzle on a bucolic train ride than while corkscrewing through the stratosphere in a Blue Angels Super Hornet.
paras.zh: 相比之下，在田园风光的火车上组装拼图游戏比乘坐蓝天使超级大黄蜂在平流层中螺旋行驶要容易得多。

paras.en: Ocean island basalts (OIBs) offer evidence of Earth's core oozing, because they're formed by upwellings from near the boundary between the core and mantle.
paras.zh: 海岛玄武岩（OIB）提供了地核渗漏的证据，因为它们是由地核和地幔边界附近的上升流形成的。

paras.en: These lavas erupt from places like Baffin Island, located in Nunavut, Canada, and from Iceland, located in Iceland.
paras.zh: 这些熔岩从位于加拿大努勒维特的巴芬岛和位于冰岛的冰岛等地喷发。

paras.en: They also appear to bring the light hydrogen accumulated from the Solar nebula that created our Solar System, a geochemical time capsule from before everything we know existed.
paras.zh: 它们似乎还带来了太阳星云中积累的轻氢，太阳星云创造了我们的太阳系，这是我们所知道的一切存在之前的一个地球化学时间胶囊。

paras.en: As this hydrogen escapes upward from the core, it enriches the mantle and lowers its D/H ratio.
paras.zh: 当氢从地核向上逃逸时，它会丰富地幔并降低其 D/H 比。

paras.en: Helium isotope ratios provide another clue, as helium-3 is a lighter, primordial isotope from the Solar nebula, much of it courtesy of the Big Bang, while the heavier helium-4 is produced by radioactive decay in Earth's upper layers.
paras.zh: 氦同位素比提供了另一条线索，因为氦 3 是一种来自太阳星云的较轻的原始同位素，大部分是由大爆炸产生的，而较重的氦 4 是由地球上层的放射性衰变产生的。

paras.en: As a result, a higher ratio of helium-3 to helium-4 in the OIBs adds further evidence that it is likewise escaping from Earth's core.
paras.zh: 因此，OIB 中氦 3 与氦 4 的比例较高，进一步证明它同样正在逃离地核。

paras.en: Tungsten offers one more crucial puzzle piece, as this heavy metal was initially sequestered in the core as Earth's layer separated into a planetary bloomin' onion during crystallization. But now an anciently exiled tungsten isotope hitches rides on rising plumes, tracing the core materials as they're regurgitated upward through Earth's guts.
paras.zh: 钨提供了一个更重要的拼图，因为当地球层在结晶过程中分离成行星开花洋葱时，这种重金属最初被隔离在核心中。但现在，一种古老的被流放的钨同位素搭乘着上升的羽流，追踪着通过地球内部向上回流的核心材料。

paras.en: So, for a nightcap-based recap, the researchers' evidence includes a triumvirate chemical cocktail from the deepest, oldest depths of our world: these hydrogen, helium, and tungsten ratios trace our leaking core.
paras.zh: 因此，对于睡前回顾，研究人员的证据包括来自我们世界最深、最古老深处的三元化学混合物：这些氢、氦和钨的比例追踪了我们泄漏的核心。

paras.en: "These findings suggest that even if primordial deep-mantle reservoirs once existed, the hydrogen isotope signatures in the present-day deep lower mantle are unlikely to represent simple relics of early differentiation," the researchers conclude.
paras.zh: 研究人员得出结论：“这些发现表明，即使原始深部地幔储层曾经存在，当今下地幔深处的氢同位素特征也不太可能代表早期分化的简单遗迹。”

paras.en: Instead, they "reflect dynamic modification by ongoing core-mantle exchange throughout Earth's evolution," the researchers conclude.
paras.zh: 相反，研究人员得出结论，它们“反映了整个地球演化过程中持续发生的地核-地幔交换的动态变化”。

paras.en: The research has been published in Science Advances.
paras.zh: 该研究已发表在《科学进展》上。

articles.title: A 24-year study uncovers a surprising climate benefit beneath forests

paras.en: A 24-year study uncovers a surprising climate benefit beneath forests
paras.zh: 一项历时 24 年的研究揭示了森林地下令人惊讶的气候效益

paras.en: Forest soils may be quietly helping fight climate change more effectively than scientists expected.
paras.zh: 森林土壤可能比科学家预期的更有效地帮助应对气候变化。

paras.en: - Scientists have discovered that some forest soils are becoming surprisingly better at removing methane from the atmosphere as temperatures rise and rainfall declines. A study spanning up to 24 years found methane absorption increasing by an average of 3% annually, challenging previous predictions about climate change's effects on forests.
paras.zh: - 科学家们发现，随着气温上升和降雨量减少，一些森林土壤在去除大气中甲烷方面出人意料地变得更好。一项长达 24 年的研究发现，甲烷吸收量平均每年增加 3%，挑战了之前关于气候变化对森林影响的预测。

paras.en: Forest soils are playing a surprisingly powerful role in removing methane from the atmosphere, and new findings suggest that certain effects of climate change could make them even better at it. Methane is a potent greenhouse gas that contributes to global warming, but microorganisms living in the soil can break it down before it builds up in the air.
paras.zh: 森林土壤在清除大气中的甲烷方面发挥着令人惊讶的强大作用，新的发现表明，气候变化的某些影响可能会让它们在这方面做得更好。甲烷是一种强效温室气体，会导致全球变暖，但生活在土壤中的微生物可以在其在空气中积聚之前将其分解。

paras.en: Scientists from the University of Göttingen and the Baden-Württemberg Forest Research Institute (FVA) analyzed the world's most comprehensive collection of long-term measurements of methane absorption by forest soils. Their findings revealed an unexpected trend: under certain climate conditions that could become more common in the future, forest soils can actually increase the amount of methane they remove from the atmosphere.
paras.zh: 哥廷根大学和巴登-符腾堡森林研究所 (FVA) 的科学家分析了世界上最全面的森林土壤甲烷吸收长期测量数据集。他们的发现揭示了一个意想不到的趋势：在未来可能变得更加普遍的某些气候条件下，森林土壤实际上可以增加从大气中清除的甲烷量。

paras.en: The researchers examined measurements collected from 13 forest sites in southwestern Germany over periods of up to 24 years. On average, the amount of methane absorbed by the soils increased by approximately 3% annually. The researchers linked this rise to declining rainfall and warmer temperatures, which create conditions that make it easier for methane to enter the soil and be broken down by microorganisms.
paras.zh: 研究人员检查了在长达 24 年的时间内从德国西南部 13 个森林地点收集的测量结果。平均而言，土壤吸收的甲烷量每年增加约3%。研究人员将这种上升与降雨量减少和气温升高联系起来，这创造了使甲烷更容易进入土壤并被微生物分解的条件。

paras.en: The findings, published in Agricultural and Forest Meteorology, challenge previous research suggesting that climate change is generally reducing the ability of forest soils to absorb methane.
paras.zh: 这项研究结果发表在《农业和森林气象学》上，对之前的研究提出了挑战，之前的研究表明气候变化普遍降低了森林土壤吸收甲烷的能力。

paras.en: How Scientists Measured Methane Absorption Over 24 Years
paras.zh: 科学家如何测量 24 年来的甲烷吸收

paras.en: To understand how methane absorption changes over time, the researchers examined an extensive collection of soil gas measurements gathered through the FVA's long-running monitoring program.
paras.zh: 为了了解甲烷吸收如何随时间变化，研究人员检查了通过 FVA 长期运行的监测计划收集的大量土壤气体测量数据。

paras.en: The measurements included soil gas profiles, which reveal the chemical composition of gases trapped in the soil at different depths. Every two weeks, researchers collected air samples through thin tubes installed beneath the ground and analyzed them in a laboratory. This repeated sampling allowed scientists to track changes in methane concentrations over many years.
paras.zh: 测量结果包括土壤气体剖面，它揭示了不同深度土壤中截留气体的化学成分。每两周，研究人员就会通过安装在地下的细管收集空气样本，并在实验室中进行分析。这种重复采样使科学家能够追踪多年来甲烷浓度的变化。

paras.en: To confirm their findings, the team also used an independent measurement technique involving airtight chambers placed directly on the soil surface. By monitoring how gas concentrations changed inside these chambers, the researchers could determine whether the soil was absorbing methane and calculate how much was being removed.
paras.zh: 为了证实他们的发现，研究小组还使用了一种独立的测量技术，涉及直接放置在土壤表面的密闭室。通过监测这些室内气体浓度的变化，研究人员可以确定土壤是否吸收了甲烷，并计算出了多少甲烷被去除。

paras.en: Combining these methods gave the scientists a detailed picture of methane uptake across the forest sites and how it responded to changing environmental conditions.
paras.zh: 结合这些方法，科学家们可以详细了解整个森林的甲烷吸收情况以及它如何应对不断变化的环境条件。

paras.en: Why Warmer, Drier Forest Soils Absorb More Methane
paras.zh: 为什么温暖、干燥的森林土壤会吸收更多的甲烷

paras.en: Although methane absorption varied considerably between the 13 locations, a clear overall pattern emerged. Forest soils in southwestern Germany were particularly effective at removing methane from the atmosphere during periods of lower rainfall and higher temperatures.
paras.zh: 尽管 13 个地点之间的甲烷吸收量差异很大，但出现了清晰的总体模式。在降雨量较少和气温较高的时期，德国西南部的森林土壤对于去除大气中的甲烷特别有效。

paras.en: "Our long-term data shows that climate change does not necessarily have a negative impact on how much methane forest soils absorb. While the largest study to date from the US found a decline in methane uptake of up to 80 percent due to increasing rainfall, our significantly more comprehensive field study in south-western Germany found the opposite, " explains Professor Martin Maier at Göttingen University's Department of Crop Sciences, who led the study and was previously involved in the FVA's soil gas monitoring program.
paras.zh: “我们的长期数据表明，气候变化并不一定会对森林土壤的甲烷吸收量产生负面影响。虽然美国迄今为止最大规模的研究发现，由于降雨量增加，甲烷吸收量下降了高达 80%，但我们在德国西南部进行的更为全面的实地研究发现了相反的结果，”领导这项研究并曾参与 FVA 土壤气体监测项目的哥廷根大学作物科学系的 Martin Maier 教授解释道。

paras.en: "We observed a significant long-term increase in methane uptake in the forest areas we studied."
paras.zh: “我们观察到我们研究的森林地区甲烷吸收量长期显着增加。”

paras.en: The explanation lies partly in how water moves through the ground. When soil becomes saturated with moisture, water fills many of the tiny spaces between soil particles, making it more difficult for gases to move through them. Drier soil contains more pores filled with air, allowing atmospheric methane to travel deeper into the ground.
paras.zh: 部分解释在于水如何穿过地面。当土壤水分饱和时，水会填充土壤颗粒之间的许多微小空间，使气体更难穿过它们。干燥的土壤含有更多充满空气的孔隙，使大气中的甲烷能够深入地下。

paras.en: Once methane enters the soil, microorganisms use it as an energy source, breaking it down in the process. Rising temperatures can slightly accelerate this microbial activity, allowing the organisms to consume methane more quickly.
paras.zh: 一旦甲烷进入土壤，微生物就会将其用作能源，并在此过程中将其分解。温度升高会稍微加速这种微生物活动，使生物体更快地消耗甲烷。

paras.en: Together, these two effects help explain why warmer temperatures and reduced rainfall were associated with greater methane absorption in the forests studied.
paras.zh: 这两种效应共同有助于解释为什么气温升高和降雨量减少与所研究的森林中甲烷吸收量增加有关。

paras.en: Findings Challenge Previous Climate Change Research
paras.zh: 研究结果挑战了之前的气候变化研究

paras.en: The results offer a different perspective from several major international research reviews. These analyses, known as meta-analyses, combine findings from numerous individual studies to identify broader patterns. Many have concluded that methane absorption by forest soils is declining.
paras.zh: 研究结果提供了与几项主要国际研究评论不同的视角。这些分析称为荟萃分析，结合了众多单独研究的结果来确定更广泛的模式。许多人得出结论，森林土壤的甲烷吸收量正在下降。

paras.en: However, the German study suggests that the relationship between climate change and methane uptake is more complicated than those overall trends indicate. While increasing rainfall can reduce methane absorption by limiting the movement of gas through soil, drier conditions can produce the opposite effect.
paras.zh: 然而，德国的研究表明，气候变化与甲烷吸收之间的关系比总体趋势所显示的更为复杂。虽然增加降雨量可以通过限制气体在土壤中的移动来减少甲烷吸收，但干燥的条件会产生相反的效果。

paras.en: The findings do not mean that climate change is beneficial for forests overall. Instead, they demonstrate that its effects on methane absorption can differ considerably depending on local temperatures, rainfall patterns, and soil conditions.
paras.zh: 研究结果并不意味着气候变化对整个森林有利。相反，他们证明，它对甲烷吸收的影响可能会因当地温度、降雨模式和土壤条件的不同而有很大差异。

paras.en: The researchers emphasize that these regional differences make long-term monitoring especially important. Shorter studies or analyses that combine measurements from widely different environments may miss gradual changes that only become apparent after years of observation.
paras.zh: 研究人员强调，这些区域差异使得长期监测尤为重要。结合来自不同环境的测量结果的较短研究或分析可能会错过只有在多年观察后才变得明显的逐渐变化。

paras.en: "Our results make it clear that taking a series of measurements over many years and running monitoring programs are indispensable for assessing the real effects of climate change," says Maier.
paras.zh: “我们的结果清楚地表明，多年来进行一系列测量并运行监测计划对于评估气候变化的实际影响是必不可少的，”迈尔说。

paras.zh: 材料由哥廷根大学提供。注意：内容的风格和长度可能会被编辑。

articles.title: NASA’s Webb reveals the wild weather of a mysterious world 20 light-years away

paras.en: NASAâs Webb reveals the wild weather of a mysterious world 20 light-years away
paras.zh: NASA 的韦伯揭示了 20 光年外神秘世界的狂野天气

paras.en: - NASAâs James Webb Space Telescope has revealed that a turbulent world 20 light-years away has a surprisingly orderly weather system, with three recurring atmospheric states driven by temperature changes and shifting clouds. The breakthrough gives scientists a powerful new tool for uncovering weather patterns on distant worlds and understanding the conditions that shape their atmospheres.
paras.zh: - NASA 的詹姆斯·韦伯太空望远镜揭示了 20 光年外的一个动荡世界拥有令人惊讶的有序天气系统，由温度变化和云层变化驱动的三种反复出现的大气状态。这一突破为科学家提供了一个强大的新工具，可以揭示遥远世界的天气模式并了解塑造其大气层的条件。

paras.en: Scientists have discovered a powerful new way to decode the weather on distant worlds, revealing surprisingly organized patterns hidden within the turbulent atmosphere of a mysterious object 20 light-years from Earth.
paras.zh: 科学家们发现了一种强大的新方法来解码遥远世界的天气，揭示了隐藏在距离地球 20 光年的神秘物体的湍流大气层中的令人惊讶的组织模式。

paras.en: Researchers at Trinity College Dublin used observations from NASA's James Webb Space Telescope to investigate SIMP 0136, a brown dwarf previously associated with phenomena resembling the northern lights. They found that its complex weather is largely governed by just two factors: changes in temperature and the vertical structure of its clouds.
paras.zh: 都柏林三一学院的研究人员利用美国宇航局詹姆斯·韦伯太空望远镜的观测结果来研究 SIMP 0136，这是一颗此前与类似北极光的现象有关的褐矮星。他们发现其复杂的天气主要由两个因素决定：温度的变化和云的垂直结构。

paras.en: The discovery offers a new way to understand the atmospheric conditions of distant worlds and could help astronomers investigate planets far beyond our Solar System.
paras.zh: 这一发现提供了一种了解遥远世界大气状况的新方法，并可以帮助天文学家研究远离太阳系的行星。

paras.en: How NASA's Webb Telescope Decoded Alien Weather
To investigate SIMP 0136, the researchers analyzed observations collected by NASA's James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) using a mathematical technique called Principal Component Analysis (PCA).
paras.zh: 为了研究 SIMP 0136，研究人员使用一种称为主成分分析 (PCA) 的数学技术分析了 NASA 詹姆斯·韦伯太空望远镜 (JWST) 收集的观测结果。

paras.en: This technique helps scientists make sense of large, complicated datasets by identifying the strongest patterns within them. In this case, the team examined how the brown dwarf's light changed as it rotated, looking for subtle variations that could reveal what was happening in its atmosphere.
paras.zh: 这项技术可以帮助科学家通过识别大型复杂数据集中最强的模式来理解数据集。在这种情况下，研究小组检查了褐矮星旋转时光线如何变化，寻找可以揭示其大气层中发生的情况的细微变化。

paras.en: Rather than beginning with detailed assumptions about how the atmosphere should behave, the researchers allowed the observations to reveal the most important processes. The method also helped separate genuine atmospheric changes from minor fluctuations and random noise in the measurements.
paras.zh: 研究人员并没有从关于大气应该如何表现的详细假设开始，而是让观测揭示了最重要的过程。该方法还有助于将真正的大气变化与测量中的微小波动和随机噪声区分开来。

paras.en: Webb's exceptionally sensitive instruments made this possible by detecting extremely small changes in the object's brightness as different parts of its atmosphere rotated into view.
paras.zh: 韦伯异常灵敏的仪器通过检测物体大气的不同部分旋转到视野中时亮度的极小变化，使这一点成为可能。

paras.en: Scientists Discover Hidden Order in Chaotic Alien Weather

The results revealed something unexpected. Although SIMP 0136 appears to have a highly complicated atmosphere, nearly all of its observed atmospheric variability could be explained by just two dominant components, consistent with temperature fluctuations and changes in the vertical arrangement of clouds.
paras.zh: 结果揭示了一些意想不到的事情。尽管 SIMP 0136 似乎拥有高度复杂的大气层，但几乎所有观测到的大气变化都可以用两个主要成分来解释，这两个成分与温度波动和云垂直排列的变化一致。

paras.en: Even more remarkably, the researchers identified three recurring weather states that appear and disappear from view as the brown dwarf rotates.
paras.zh: 更值得注意的是，研究人员发现了三种反复出现的天气状态，它们随着褐矮星的旋转而出现和消失。

paras.en: Together, these states create a shifting atmospheric patchwork. Some regions are hotter and have thinner clouds, while others are cooler and contain thicker cloud layers that extend farther vertically through the atmosphere.
paras.zh: 这些状态共同创造出不断变化的大气拼凑物。有些地区较热，云层较薄，而另一些地区则较冷，云层较厚，云层在大气中垂直延伸得更远。

paras.en: Instead of constantly changing in an unpredictable way, these weather patterns appear to follow an underlying structure.
paras.zh: 这些天气模式并不是以不可预测的方式不断变化，而是遵循一个潜在的结构。

paras.en: The findings, published in Astronomy & Astrophysics, suggest that the seemingly chaotic atmosphere of SIMP 0136 is actually governed by a remarkably consistent set of processes.
paras.zh: 发表在《天文学与天体物理学》上的研究结果表明，SIMP 0136 看似混乱的大气实际上是由一组非常一致的过程控制的。

paras.en: Brown dwarfs occupy an unusual place between planets and stars. SIMP 0136 is larger and hotter than a typical gas giant planet, but it lacks the mass needed to shine like a star. Its atmosphere contains enormous cloud systems that evolve rapidly, making its weather more comparable to an extreme version of Jupiter's than anything experienced on Earth.
paras.zh: 褐矮星在行星和恒星之间占据着一个不寻常的位置。 SIMP 0136 比典型的气态巨行星更大、更热，但它缺乏像恒星一样发光所需的质量。它的大气层包含快速演化的巨大云系统，使其天气比地球上经历过的任何天气都更接近木星的极端版本​​。

paras.en: These immense weather systems can span planetary scales, continually changing the appearance of the distant world.
paras.zh: 这些巨大的天气系统可以跨越行星尺度，不断改变遥远世界的面貌。

paras.en: "We also discovered that these drivers of the weather patterns on SIMP-0136 persist over time, even as the detailed appearance of the atmosphere evolves over more than a dozen rotations," said first author Merle Schrader, a PhD candidate in Trinity's School of Physics.
paras.zh: “我们还发现，SIMP-0136 上的这些天气模式驱动因素会随着时间的推移而持续存在，即使大气的详细外观经过十几次旋转而演变，”第一作者、三一物理学院的博士生梅尔·施拉德 (Merle Schrader) 说。

paras.en: "In relative terms, SIMP 0136 is one of the easier brown dwarfs for us to capture high-quality data from. These data have been studied before by established methods, allowing us to compare some of the results from this new technique to what we already know about this object. The technique has also helped us develop a better understanding of what drives the weather on this faraway world and how these weather patterns interact and co-exist, but perhaps even more importantly, it shows how this approach can be further refined and applied to other, less well-known brown dwarfs in different parts of space."
paras.zh: “相对而言，SIMP 0136 是我们更容易捕获高质量数据的褐矮星之一。这些数据之前已经通过既定方法进行了研究，使我们能够将这项新技术的一些结果与我们已经了解的有关该天体的信息进行比较。该技术还帮助我们更好地了解驱动这个遥远世界天气的因素以及这些天气模式如何相互作用和共存，但也许更重要的是，它展示了如何进一步完善这种方法并将其应用于其他较小的星球。太空不同部分的著名褐矮星。”

paras.en: A Remarkable Connection Across 20 Light Years
paras.zh: 跨越 20 光年的非凡联系

paras.en: For Schrader, the research also revealed an extraordinary personal connection to the distant object.
paras.zh: 对于施拉德来说，这项研究还揭示了与这个遥远物体之间非同寻常的个人联系。

paras.en: SIMP 0136 is located approximately 20 light years from Earth, meaning its light takes about two decades to reach us. The light captured by Webb in 2023, which provided the observations used in the study, had actually left the brown dwarf during the year Schrader was born.
paras.zh: SIMP 0136 距离地球约 20 光年，这意味着它的光需要大约二十年才能到达我们。韦伯在 2023 年捕获的光线（提供了研究中使用的观测结果）实际上是在施拉德出生的那一年离开了褐矮星。

paras.en: "Light travels at around 300,000 km/s but, even at that speed, it took two decades to reach us, peering through the JWST lenses," she said.
paras.zh: “光的传播速度约为 300,000 公里/秒，但即使以这样的速度，通过 JWST 镜头观察，也需要二十年才能到达我们，”她说。

paras.en: "When you consider light takes just over a second to reach the Moon after leaving Earth, that gives a sense of how far away SIMP 0136 is, and how incredible astrophysical progress has been. I think it's amazing that we have been able to discern the intimate weather patterns of a distant world and map their interactions from our cozy little corner of the universe, when all we observe directly of these objects is a single pixel spread across the light spectrum."
paras.zh: “当你考虑到光离开地球后只需要一秒钟多一点的时间就能到达月球，这就让人感觉到 SIMP 0136 有多远，以及天体物理学的进步是多么令人难以置信。我认为，当我们直接观察到这些物体的只是分布在光谱上的单个像素时，我们能够辨别遥远世界的亲密天气模式并从我们舒适的宇宙小角落绘制它们的相互作用，这是令人惊奇的。”

paras.en: The achievement highlights how much information astronomers can extract from seemingly tiny amounts of light. Even though SIMP 0136 appears as little more than a single point in telescope observations, changes in its brightness at different wavelengths can reveal detailed information about its atmosphere.
paras.zh: 这一成就凸显了天文学家可以从看似微量的光中提取出多少信息。尽管 SIMP 0136 在望远镜观测中看起来只不过是一个点，但它在不同波长下的亮度变化可以揭示有关其大气的详细信息。

paras.en: What This Discovery Means for Distant Planets
paras.zh: 这一发现对遥远的行星意味着什么

paras.en: The new technique could have implications far beyond SIMP 0136.
paras.zh: 这项新技术的影响可能远远超出 SIMP 0136。

paras.en: Brown dwarfs are particularly valuable for investigating the atmospheres of giant exoplanets, which are planets orbiting stars outside our Solar System. Because brown dwarfs can often be observed directly, they give scientists an opportunity to study atmospheric processes that are much harder to investigate on most exoplanets.
paras.zh: 褐矮星对于研究巨型系外行星的大气层特别有价值，系外行星是太阳系外绕恒星运行的行星。由于褐矮星通常可以直接观测到，因此它们为科学家提供了研究大气过程的机会，而这在大多数系外行星上很难研究。

paras.en: By examining these objects, researchers can test how clouds form, how heat moves through an atmosphere, and how atmospheric circulation behaves under extreme conditions.
paras.zh: 通过检查这些物体，研究人员可以测试云是如何形成的、热量如何在大气中移动以及大气环流在极端条件下如何表现。

paras.en: The technique developed by the Trinity team could make those investigations considerably more efficient. By quickly identifying the processes responsible for most of the observed atmospheric changes, astronomers can better determine which features deserve closer examination using more complicated computer models.
paras.zh: Trinity 团队开发的技术可以大大提高这些调查的效率。通过快速识别导致大多数观测到的大气变化的过程，天文学家可以更好地确定哪些特征值得使用更复杂的计算机模型进行更仔细的检查。

paras.en: Professor Johanna Vos, Associate Professor in Trinity School of Physics, explained the potential significance of the findings.
paras.zh: 三一物理学院副教授 Johanna Vos 解释了这一发现的潜在意义。

paras.en: "Our findings will transform how astronomers analyze future JWST observations. Since our approach rapidly identifies the dominant components of the atmosphere it offers an efficient first step before we begin computationally intensive modeling.
paras.zh: “我们的发现将改变天文学家分析未来 JWST 观测结果的方式。由于我们的方法可以快速识别大气的主要成分，因此它为我们开始计算密集型建模提供了有效的第一步。

paras.en: "Applying this technique to a wide range of brown dwarfs and giant exoplanets will help us better understand the diverse weather systems that shape worlds far beyond our Solar System."
paras.zh: “将这项技术应用于广泛的褐矮星和巨型系外行星将有助于我们更好地了解塑造太阳系以外世界的多样化天气系统。”

paras.en: Ultimately, understanding weather on distant worlds is about more than identifying clouds and temperature changes. Atmospheric behavior can provide important clues about a planet's chemical composition, physical conditions, and overall environment.
paras.zh: 最终，了解遥远世界的天气不仅仅是识别云层和温度变化。大气行为可以提供有关行星化学成分、物理条件和整体环境的重要线索。

paras.en: Those insights are also relevant to one of astronomy's biggest questions: which planets beyond our Solar System might have conditions capable of supporting life?
paras.zh: 这些见解也与天文学最大的问题之一相关：太阳系以外的哪些行星可能具备支持生命存在的条件？

paras.en: By revealing how complex alien atmospheres can be understood from faint changes in light, this new approach could help scientists take another step toward answering that question.
paras.zh: 通过揭示如何从微弱的光线变化来理解复杂的外星大气，这种新方法可以帮助科学家在回答这个问题上又迈出一步。

paras.en: Materials provided by Trinity College Dublin. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
paras.zh: 材料由都柏林三一学院提供。注意：内容的风格和长度可能会被编辑。
