paras.zh: 如果您信赖我们团队的可信报道，请花点时间选择我们作为您在 Google 上的首选来源，这样您始终会首先看到我们经过验证的新闻。

articles.title: Ilhan Omar: The US Democrat targeted by Donald Trump

paras.en: "Ilhan Omar, whatever the hell her name is, with the little – with the little turban, I love her. She comes in, does nothing but bitch."
paras.zh: “伊尔汗·奥马尔，不管她叫什么名字，带着小头巾，带着小头巾，我爱她。她进来，除了婊子什么也不做。”

paras.en: "Ilhan Omar is garbage. She's garbage. Her friends are garbage. […] These aren't people that work. These aren't people that say, let's go. Come on, let's make this place great. These are people that do nothing but complain."
paras.zh: “伊尔汗·奥马尔是垃圾。她是垃圾。她的朋友也是垃圾。[……]这些人不工作。这些人不会说，我们走吧。来吧，让我们让这个地方变得伟大。这些人除了抱怨什么也不做。”

paras.en: "She comes in from a country without laws, without police, without military, where all they do is shoot each other. And she comes into our country, and she says, 'I have a constitutional right.' She's telling us about the constitution, and she comes from one of the worst countries anywhere on the planet."
paras.zh: “她来自一个没有法律、没有警察、没有军队的国家，他们所做的就是互相开枪。她来到我们的国家，她说，‘我有宪法权利。’”她正在向我们讲述宪法，而她来自地球上最糟糕的国家之一。”

paras.en: These are just three of Donald Trump's many attacks on US Democratic congresswoman Ilhan Omar. Few people have been targeted as ferociously by the US president. But why has Trump singled her out for such hostility?
paras.zh: 这些只是唐纳德·特朗普对美国民主党女议员伊尔汗·奥马尔的多次攻击中的三项。很少有人像美国总统那样猛烈地攻击目标。但特朗普为什么要对她表现出如此敌意呢？

paras.en: Ilhan Abdullahi Omar, 44, was born in Mogadishu, the capital of Somalia. She fled the civil war in the country while still a child, and spent four years in a refugee camp in Kenya. She finally came with her family to the US in 1995, at the age of 12, and became a US citizen in 2000. She joined the Democratic Party, and made a career as a politician on the party's left wing. Since January 2019, she has served as representative for the state of Minnesota and one of the first two Muslim women to enter the US Congress.
paras.zh: 伊尔汗·阿卜杜拉希·奥马尔，44 岁，出生于索马里首都摩加迪沙。当她还是个孩子的时候，她就逃离了该国的内战，并在肯尼亚的难民营度过了四年。 1995年，12岁的她终于随家人来到美国，并于2000年成为美国公民。她加入民主党，并成为该党左翼政治家。自2019年1月起，她担任明尼苏达州代表，也是首批进入美国国会的两名穆斯林女性之一。

paras.en: Ilhan Omar is a practising Muslim who wears a hijab, and Congress altered a 180-year-old rule for her that prohibited head coverings in the chamber of the House of Representatives. Politically and socially, Omar champions progressive values, and often makes a connection between her faith and her commitment to social justice, human rights, and the protection of minorities.
paras.zh: 伊尔汗·奥马尔 (Ilhan Omar) 是一名戴头巾的虔诚穆斯林，国会为她修改了一项已有 180 年历史的规定，即禁止在众议院会议厅戴头巾。在政治和社会上，奥马尔倡导进步价值观，并经常将她的信仰与她对社会正义、人权和保护少数群体的承诺联系起来。

paras.en: Omar campaigns on issues such as universal health insurance, increasing the minimum wage, climate protection, and the cancellation of student debt. She is also one of Donald Trump's most prominent and outspoken critics, repeatedly accusing him of racism and systematically fomenting hatred against minorities, immigrants, and Muslims. She has frequently condemned raids by the US Immigration and Customs Enforcement agency (ICE), which she describes as a "militarized campaign of fear." She has also accused the president of corruption in office.
paras.zh: 奥马尔就全民健康保险、提高最低工资、气候保护和取消学生债务等问题开展竞选活动。她也是唐纳德·特朗普最著名、最直言不讳的批评者之一，多次指责他种族主义，并系统地煽动针对少数族裔、移民和穆斯林的仇恨。她经常谴责美国移民和海关执法局（ICE）的突袭行动，她将其描述为“军事化的恐惧运动”。她还指责总统在任内腐败。

paras.en: Criticism of Israel and accusations of antisemitism
paras.zh: 对以色列的批评和反犹太主义的指控

paras.en: Young, outspoken, female, Muslim, and a left-wing Democrat – politically, Ilhan Omar is almost the polar opposite of the 80-year-old Republican Trump. But she is also a controversial figure within her own party.
paras.zh: 年轻、直言不讳、女性、穆斯林和左翼民主党人——在政治上，伊尔汗·奥马尔几乎与 80 岁的共和党人特朗普截然相反。但她在自己的党内也是一个有争议的人物。

paras.en: Omar is one of the fiercest critics of Israel in US politics, and has repeatedly called Washington's support for the country into question. She has been accused of antisemitism, and of supporting the movement BDS (Boycott, Divestment and Sanctions), which encourages people to boycott Israeli businesses. Omar has defended BDS as a legitimate form of non-violent protest and freedom of expression. In 2019, she even introduced a resolution in the US Congress that aimed to strengthen the right of Americans to boycott, with a view to countering laws that restrict what the BDS movement can do.
paras.zh: 奥马尔是美国政坛对以色列最激烈的批评者之一，并多次质疑华盛顿对该国的支持。她被指控反犹太主义，并支持 BDS（抵制、撤资和制裁）运动，该运动鼓励人们抵制以色列企业。奥马尔捍卫 BDS 是非暴力抗议和言论自由的合法形式。 2019年，她甚至在美国国会提出一项决议，旨在加强美国人抵制的权利，以期对抗限制BDS运动活动的法律。

paras.en: In early 2023, Republicans removed her from the House Foreign Affairs Committee over a number of controversial tweets, including a comment she made in 2021 that seemed to equate the actions of the US and Israel with those of the Taliban in Afghanistan, and the Palestinian group Hamas. The latter is classified as a terrorist organization by the US and many other countries around the world.
paras.zh: 2023 年初，共和党因一系列有争议的推文而将她从众议院外交事务委员会除名，其中包括她在 2021 年发表的一条评论，该评论似乎将美国和以色列的行动与阿富汗塔利班和巴勒斯坦组织哈马斯的行动等同起来。后者被美国和世界许多其他国家列为恐怖组织。

paras.en: Accusations of embezzlement and immigration fraud
paras.zh: 贪污和移民欺诈指控

paras.en: Her critics also tried to link Omar to a corruption scandal in her home state of Minnesota. During the COVID-19 pandemic, around $250 million (€220 million) were misappropriated from a government-funded food program for children. Omar had previously called for the rules of the program to be eased.
paras.zh: 她的批评者还试图将奥马尔与她家乡明尼苏达州的腐败丑闻联系起来。在 COVID-19 大流行期间，政府资助的儿童食品计划中约有 2.5 亿美元（2.2 亿欧元）被挪用。奥马尔此前曾呼吁放宽该计划的规则。

paras.en: Many of those convicted were from the state's Somali community, something that political opponents, including Trump, seized on to claim Omar was involved. No law enforcement authorities have ever accused her of any wrongdoing.
paras.zh: 许多被定罪的人来自该州的索马里社区，包括特朗普在内的政治对手抓住这一点声称奥马尔参与其中。没有执法机构指控她有任何不当行为。

paras.en: The most recent accusation against Omar concerns her immigration to the US. For years, her opponents have claimed that she made false statements during the procedure, even alleging that she entered into a fraudulent marriage with her biological brother to help him secure a US visa. On October 12, federal officials ordered a search of Omar's home, investigating allegations that Omar's father lied about her age on her immigration application.
paras.zh: 针对奥马尔的最新指控涉及她移民美国。多年来，她的反对者一直声称她在手术过程中做出了虚假陈述，甚至声称她与亲生兄弟进行了欺诈婚姻，以帮助他获得美国签证。 10 月 12 日，联邦官员下令搜查奥马尔的家，调查奥马尔父亲在她的移民申请中谎报年龄的指控。

paras.en: Omar has repeatedly denied the accusations, describing them as part of a "campaign of political intimidation" and "an attempt to target political enemies." Several leading Democratic politicians have come to her defense, accusing the Trump administration of weaponizing the Justice Department and Department of Homeland Security against its political opponents.
paras.zh: 奥马尔一再否认这些指控，称其为“政治恐吓运动”和“针对政敌的企图”的一部分。几位主要的民主党政界人士为她辩护，指责特朗普政府将司法部和国土安全部武器化以对付其政治对手。

paras.en: Former immigration officials told the Reuters news agency that it is extremely unusual for a house search to be conducted as part of such an investigation, as the government should already have all the relevant immigration documents.
paras.zh: 前移民官员告诉路透社，作为此类调查的一部分进行房屋搜查是极其不寻常的，因为政府应该已经拥有所有相关的移民文件。

paras.en: Many see a raid on the home of a sitting member of Congress over a formality from 26 years ago as excessive, and have been especially critical of the timing of the raid, just three weeks before the Congressional elections in which Omar is standing for re-election.
paras.zh: 许多人认为，26 年前因手续而对一名现任国会议员的住所进行突击搜查是过分的，并且对这次突击搜查的时机尤其批评，当时距离奥马尔竞选连任的国会选举仅三周。

paras.en: The long-standing, unwritten "60-Day Rule" holds that authorities do not take any public action against political candidates in the two months before an election, so as not to influence the outcome. Critics see the fact that this practice has been ignored in Omar's case as amounting to election interference.
paras.zh: 长期以来不成文的“60天规则”规定，当局在选举前两个月内不得对政治候选人采取任何公开行动，以免影响结果。批评者认为，这种做法在奥马尔的案件中被忽视，构成了选举干预。

paras.en: With the midterm electionslooming, Trump is battling with plummeting approval ratings, and Omar is not the only Muslim politician the president has been attacking. Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic candidate in the Senate election in Michigan, is another.
paras.zh: 随着中期选举的临近，特朗普正在与支持率暴跌作斗争，而奥马尔并不是总统唯一攻击的穆斯林政治家。密歇根州参议院选举的民主党候选人阿卜杜勒·赛义德（Abdul El-Sayed）是另一个例子。

paras.en: At a rally last Saturday in Tennessee, Trump said of El-Sayed: "I call him Mohammed. Somebody said, 'His name isn't Mohammed, it's Abdul.' I said, 'To me, it's Mohammed.' I'm the president. I can call him whatever the hell I want. To me, he's Mohammed, and he's a radical jihadist."
paras.zh: 上周六在田纳西州的一次集会上，特朗普谈到埃尔-赛义德时说道：“我称他为穆罕默德。有人说，‘他的名字不是穆罕默德，而是阿卜杜勒。’”我说，“对我来说，就是穆罕默德。”我是总统。我可以随心所欲地称呼他。对我来说，他是穆罕默德，他是一名激进的圣战分子。”

paras.en: There is no intelligence whatsoever to suggest that El-Sayed has any extremist connections. The 41-year-old epidemiologist was born and brought up in Michigan. He went to university there, then won a Rhodes scholarship to Oxford, where he gained a doctorate in public health. For many years, he was the health director of the city of Detroit. Like Omar, he too belongs to the progressive left wing of the US Democratic Party.
paras.zh: 没有任何情报表明埃尔-赛义德与极端主义有任何联系。这位 41 岁的流行病学家在密歇根州出生并长大。他在那里上大学，然后获得罗德奖学金前往牛津大学，在那里他获得了公共卫生博士学位。多年来，他担任底特律市卫生总监。和奥马尔一样，他也属于美国民主党的进步左翼。

paras.en: During the election campaign, El-Sayed has repeatedly emphasized that he is not the one responsible for the rise in food prices, the expensive rents, and other political grievances. He has placed the blame squarely on what he describes as the failed policies of the administration in Washington.
paras.zh: 赛义德在竞选期间多次强调，他不是食品价格上涨、租金昂贵和其他政治不满的责任人。他将责任直接归咎于他所说的华盛顿政府的失败政策。

paras.en: This article has been translated from German.
paras.zh: 本文是从德文翻译而来。

articles.title: Search continues for 11 missing after boat sank off Mexico’s Baja coast

paras.en: The search continues for 11 people still missing after a boat capsized off Mexico’s Baja California coast on Friday, as multiple survivors have been treated for suspected shark bites, according to the US coastguard.
paras.zh: 据美国海岸警卫队称，周五，一艘船在墨西哥下加利福尼亚州海岸倾覆，目前仍有 11 人失踪，多名幸存者因疑似被鲨鱼咬伤而接受治疗。

paras.en: “Several of the individuals rescued were suffering from severe injuries consistent with shark bites, and the Coast Guard provided life-saving first aid while en route [to] San Diego,” the coastguard said in a statement on Saturday.
paras.zh: 海岸警卫队在周六的一份声明中表示：“获救的几人受到了与鲨鱼咬伤相同的重伤，海岸警卫队在前往圣地亚哥的途中提供了救生急救。”

paras.en: Sixteen Mexican nationals were rescued on Friday. Survivors told officials there were 27 people on board.
paras.zh: 周五，十六名墨西哥国民获救。幸存者告诉官员，机上有 27 人。

paras.en: The coastguard and US Navy used multiple aircraft and boats, along with assistance from the Mexican Navy, to search the area for the remaining passengers. An additional helicopter will be deployed later on Saturday, according to the coastguard.
paras.zh: 海岸警卫队和美国海军在墨西哥海军的协助下动用了多架飞机和船只，在该地区搜寻剩余的乘客。据海岸警卫队称，周六晚些时候将部署另外一架直升机。

paras.en: A Mayday call was transmitted from someone on the boat at about 1am on Friday, coastguard Lieutenant Santiago Tamburini said on the day.
paras.zh: 海岸警卫队中尉圣地亚哥·坦布里尼当天表示，周五凌晨 1 点左右，船上有人发出求救信号。

paras.en: A rescue helicopter reached the site about two hours later. It took about 90 minutes for the crew, which included a rescue swimmer, to pull the 16 people from the water, he added.
paras.zh: 大约两小时后，一架救援直升机抵达现场。他补充说，包括一名救援游泳者在内的工作人员花了大约 90 分钟将 16 人从水中救了出来。

paras.en: The boat went down about 225km (140 miles) west of Ensenada, Mexico, an area popular with fishing and leisure boats, but that is also frequented by smugglers.
paras.zh: 这艘船在墨西哥恩塞纳达以西约 225 公里（140 英里）处沉没，该地区是钓鱼和休闲船的热门地区，但也是走私者经常光顾的地方。

paras.en: Although the incident did not happen in US waters, coastguard official Charlie Valor said on Saturday they “were able to help, and that’s why we launched our assets”.
paras.zh: 尽管该事件并未发生在美国水域，但海岸警卫队官员查理·瓦洛尔周六表示，他们“能够提供帮助，这就是我们启动资产的原因”。

paras.en: Fatal attempts to transport refugees and migrants from Mexico to the US have occurred in the past.
paras.zh: 过去曾发生过试图将难民和移民从墨西哥运送到美国的致命事件。

paras.en: In May 2025, at least three people died when a boat flipped off the coast about 56km (35 miles) north of the US-Mexico border.
paras.zh: 2025 年 5 月，一艘船在美墨边境以北约 56 公里（35 英里）处的海岸翻覆，造成至少 3 人死亡。

paras.en: In 2023, eight people were killed in one of the deadliest maritime smuggling accidents off the US coast, when two boats approached a San Diego beach in heavy fog, and one capsized in the surf.
paras.zh: 2023 年，美国海岸最致命的海上走私事故之一造成 8 人死亡，当时两艘船在大雾中接近圣地亚哥海滩，其中一艘在海浪中倾覆。

articles.title: Tunisia’s economic crisis deepens as the promise of a better life fades

paras.en: Tunis, Tunisia – Like many Tunisian university graduates, Cherine Ghanmi believed a degree would offer her family a way out of poverty.
paras.zh: 突尼斯，突尼斯——和许多突尼斯大学毕业生一样，Cherine Ghanmi 相信学位将为她的家人提供摆脱贫困的出路。

paras.en: Growing up in the marginalised town of al-Mazzunah, in the central Sidi Bou Zid governorate, Ghanmi had walked 5km (3.1 miles) to the school her parents struggled to put her through. They hoped she would eventually find a job and support them financially, easing their burden after years of sacrifice.
paras.zh: 甘米在西迪布齐德省中部的边缘小镇马祖纳长大，她步行 5 公里（3.1 英里）到达她父母费尽心思送她上学的学校。他们希望她最终能找到一份工作并在经济上支持他们，减轻他们多年牺牲后的负担。

paras.en: But more than a decade after graduating in 2012, she remains unemployed. Instead of supporting her parents, she says, she continues to rely on them.
paras.zh: 但2012年毕业十多年后，她仍然失业。她说，她没有支持父母，而是继续依赖他们。

paras.en: “We studied and graduated believing we had finally found a way out of poverty,” she said. “We thought that once we found jobs, we could make up for all that hardship, repay our parents for their sacrifices and make them happy.”
paras.zh: “我们学习并毕业时相信我们终于找到了摆脱贫困的出路，”她说。 “我们以为一旦找到工作，就可以弥补所有的辛苦，报答父母的牺牲，让他们幸福。”

paras.en: “Unfortunately, reality was a big shock for us,” she added. “Instead of helping them, we have burdened them even more.”
paras.zh: “不幸的是，现实对我们来说是一个巨大的打击，”她补充道。 “我们非但没有帮助他们，反而给他们带来了更多负担。”

paras.en: For Ghanmi and thousands of other unemployed university graduates, the struggle to find work has become a symbol of Tunisia’s wider economic crisis, marked by limited opportunities, mounting financial pressure and growing frustration with successive governments.
paras.zh: 对于甘米和其他数千名失业大学毕业生来说，找工作的困难已经成为突尼斯更广泛的经济危机的象征，其特点是机会有限、财务压力不断加大以及对历届政府的不满情绪日益加剧。

paras.en: On September 27, unemployed university graduates began a roughly 300km (186-mile) march from Menzel Bouzaiane in central Tunisia towards the capital, Tunis, to demand jobs and the implementation of legislation intended to provide a clear path to public-sector employment.
paras.zh: 9 月 27 日，失业的大学毕业生开始从突尼斯中部的 Menzel Bouzaiane 向首都突尼斯游行约 300 公里（186 英里），要求提供就业机会并实施旨在为公共部门就业提供明确道路的立法。

paras.en: Known as the “Dignity March”, it began with 23 participants, according to organisers. More graduates joined along the route, with the coordinating committee later estimating that the number had grown to more than 120.
paras.zh: 据组织者称，此次游行被称为“尊严游行”，共有 23 名参与者参加。沿途有更多毕业生加入，协调委员会后来估计人数已增至 120 多人。

paras.en: The journey was physically demanding. Participants paused at points because of exhaustion and injuries before continuing towards the capital.
paras.zh: 这段旅程对体力要求很高。参与者因疲惫和受伤而在一些地方停下来，然后继续前往首都。

paras.en: On October 6, police blocked the group from moving forward in the town of Borj Cedria, south of Tunis. Participants said they were told they could travel individually, but not as a group. The marchers had hoped to reach the Tunis suburb of Carthage, where the presidential palace is located, to press their demands.
paras.zh: 10月6日，警方阻止这群人在突尼斯南部的Borj Cedria镇继续前进。参与者表示，他们被告知可以单独旅行，但不能团体旅行。游行者原本希望到达总统府所在的突尼斯郊区迦太基，以表达他们的要求。

paras.en: For Ghanmi, “the Dignity March was not just a march”, she said, describing it as an expression of the hardship and disappointment experienced by graduates who had spent years searching for work.
paras.zh: 对于甘米来说，“尊严游行不仅仅是一次游行”，她说，她将其描述为毕业生多年来寻找工作所经历的艰辛和失望的表达。

paras.en: Many protesters say they have waited years for promises of public-sector recruitment to translate into real opportunities.
paras.zh: 许多抗议者表示，他们多年来一直等待公共部门招聘的承诺转化为真正的机会。

paras.en: Their demands came amid broader discontent over Tunisia’s economic and political direction.
paras.zh: 他们的要求是在人们对突尼斯的经济和政治方向更广泛的不满之际提出的。

paras.en: On October 17, thousands gathered in Tunis to protest against President Kais Saied’s government, deteriorating living conditions and restrictions on freedoms. The demonstration, led by the Tunisian General Labour Union (UGTT), opposition groups and civil society organisations, was among the largest against Saied in years.
paras.zh: 10月17日，数千人聚集在突尼斯，抗议总统凯斯·赛义德的政府，抗议恶化的生活条件和对自由的限制。这次示威活动由突尼斯总工会（UGTT）、反对派团体和民间社会组织领导，是多年来针对赛义德最大规模的示威活动之一。

paras.en: Participants voiced frustration over unemployment and the difficulties many households face in meeting their basic needs.
paras.zh: 与会者对失业和许多家庭在满足基本需求方面面临的困难表示沮丧。

paras.en: Saied, who has concentrated power since 2021, has presented his political project as a response to corruption and the failures of the established political class. Critics say the concentration of power has weakened democratic checks and balances while doing little to resolve the country’s economic problems.
paras.zh: 自 2021 年以来权力集中的赛义德提出了他的政治计划，作为对腐败和现有政治阶层失败的回应。批评人士称，权力集中削弱了民主制衡，同时对解决该国的经济问题无济于事。

paras.en: The unemployment figures reflect the scale of the challenge. According to Tunisia’s National Institute of Statistics (INS), the overall unemployment rate stood at 14.9 percent in the second quarter of 2026. Among university graduates, it was 26.6 percent. The rate for women graduates was 35.6 percent, compared with 14.2 percent for men. Among those aged 15 to 24, unemployment reached 35.4 percent.
paras.zh: 失业数据反映了挑战的规模。根据突尼斯国家统计局（INS）的数据，2026年第二季度整体失业率为14.9%。大学毕业生的失业率为26.6%。女性毕业生率为 35.6%，而男性毕业生率为 14.2%。在15岁至24岁的人群中，失业率达到35.4%。

paras.en: “Almost all the governments that succeeded one another after the [2011] revolution did not make the economic situation, development and the treatment of social issues real priorities,” Cherif Khraifi, spokesperson for the Tunisian Union of Higher Education Graduates, told Al Jazeera.
paras.zh: 突尼斯高等教育毕业生联盟发言人谢里夫·赫莱菲 (Cherif Khraifi) 告诉半岛电视台：“[2011]革命后几乎所有接替的政府都没有将经济形势、发展和社会问题的处理作为真正的优先事项。”

paras.en: “Their biggest concern was ensuring they stayed in power.”
paras.zh: “他们最关心的是确保自己继续掌权。”

paras.en: Attempts to address graduate unemployment have repeatedly raised expectations. The 2022 Law No. 38 intended to establish an employment pathway for long-term unemployed university graduates, but the law’s implementation stalled amid financial constraints.
paras.zh: 解决毕业生失业问题的努力一再提高了人们的期望。 2022年第38号法旨在为长期失业的大学毕业生建立就业通道，但由于财政紧张，该法的实施陷入停滞。

paras.en: Khraifi said measures intended to address the crisis have too often served as “tools for letting off steam” rather than resolving the problem.
paras.zh: 卡莱菲表示，旨在解决危机的措施往往成为“发泄情绪的工具”，而不是解决问题。

paras.en: The 2025 Law No. 18 provides for the exceptional recruitment of long-term unemployed university graduates into the public sector and civil service. It calls for a digital platform to register eligible applicants and sets out criteria for prioritising candidates. Recruitment is to take place in phases over no more than three years from the law’s publication.
paras.zh: 2025 年第 18 号法律规定，公共部门和公务员部门可以例外招聘长期失业的大学毕业生。它要求建立一个数字平台来注册合格的申请人，并制定优先考虑候选人的标准。招聘将在该法律发布后不超过三年的时间内分阶段进行。

paras.en: The law was dated 22 December 2025 and published in Tunisia’s Official Gazette on 23 December 2025, when it entered into force. Article 6 provides for recruitment in phases over a period not exceeding three years from the date of publication.
paras.zh: 该法律日期为 2025 年 12 月 22 日，并于 2025 年 12 月 23 日在突尼斯官方公报上公布，并于当日生效。第六条规定，自公布之日起，在不超过三年的期限内分阶段招募。

paras.en: The graduates taking part in the Dignity March have demanded a clear process for implementing the law, including practical arrangements and a timetable for recruitment. For people who have already spent years out of work, another promise offers little reassurance without concrete steps towards employment.
paras.zh: 参加尊严游行的毕业生要求制定明确的法律实施程序，包括实际安排和招聘时间表。对于已经失业多年的人来说，如果没有具体的就业步骤，再做出的承诺也无法带来多少安慰。

paras.en: Ghanmi is also sceptical of Saied’s community-based companies programme, which aims to promote local development and employment through projects established by people in their communities.
paras.zh: 甘米还对赛义德的社区公司计划持怀疑态度，该计划旨在通过社区居民建立的项目促进当地发展和就业。

paras.en: “The authorities insist on promoting community companies as a solution for jobs and development, yet none of these companies managed to do that,” she said.
paras.zh: “当局坚持推动社区公司作为就业和发展的解决方案，但这些公司都没有做到这一点，”她说。

paras.en: Public-sector recruitment alone cannot resolve a problem of this scale, Khraifi argued. Tunisia also needs investment and businesses capable of expanding and hiring. In disadvantaged regions, where employment is scarce and access to capital is limited, starting a business can be difficult.
paras.zh: 赫莱菲认为，仅靠公共部门招聘无法解决如此规模的问题。突尼斯还需要投资以及能够扩大和雇用人才的企业。在就业机会稀缺、资金来源有限的贫困地区，创业可能会很困难。

paras.en: For graduates such as Ghanmi, the central question is whether government policies will translate into actual jobs.
paras.zh: 对于像甘米这样的毕业生来说，核心问题是政府政策是否会转化为实际工作。

paras.en: An economy struggling to create opportunities
paras.zh: 努力创造机会的经济体

paras.en: Anis Ben Said, a tax adviser and university professor, said Tunisia’s “problem is not a lack of skills, but the economy’s inability to turn skills into production, investment and job opportunities”.
paras.zh: 税务顾问兼大学教授阿尼斯·本·赛义德表示，突尼斯的“问题不是缺乏技能，而是经济无法将技能转化为生产、投资和就业机会”。

paras.en: Weak investment has constrained the creation of businesses and jobs, he told Al Jazeera. Poor infrastructure and unreliable public services also make it harder for businesses to operate, particularly in regions already struggling to attract investment.
paras.zh: 他告诉半岛电视台，投资疲软限制了企业和就业机会的创造。落后的基础设施和不可靠的公共服务也使企业经营更加困难，特别是在已经难以吸引投资的地区。

paras.en: According to the INS, Tunisia’s economy grew by 2.7 percent in 2025 and by 2.4 percent in the first half of 2026. In September, the World Bank projected growth of 2.3 percent for the full year.
paras.zh: 据INS数据，突尼斯经济2025年增长2.7%，2026年上半年增长2.4%。9月，世界银行预计全年增长2.3%。

paras.en: But economic growth does not necessarily create enough jobs for those who need them. For unemployed graduates, the figures offer little reassurance unless growth translates into accessible employment opportunities.
paras.zh: 但经济增长并不一定能为有需要的人创造足够的就业机会。对于失业的毕业生来说，这些数字并不能让人放心，除非经济增长转化为就业机会。

paras.en: “The financial crisis explains part of the problem, but it does not justify all of it,” Ben Said said.
paras.zh: “金融危机解释了部分问题，但并不能证明全部问题的合理性，”本·赛义德说。

paras.en: He pointed to shortcomings in investment and the management and maintenance of public infrastructure as barriers to economic activity.
paras.zh: 他指出投资以及公共基础设施管理和维护方面的缺陷是经济活动的障碍。

paras.en: “Infrastructure investment is not just a public expense, it is a productive economic investment,” he said
paras.zh: 他说：“基础设施投资不仅仅是一项公共开支，更是一项生产性经济投资。”

paras.en: This summer, extreme heat coincided with electricity cuts and water shortages in several parts of Tunisia. Disruptions to these basic services affected businesses and added to public frustration.
paras.zh: 今年夏天，突尼斯部分地区极端炎热，同时出现断电和缺水。这些基本服务的中断影响了企业并加剧了公众的不满。

paras.en: The Reuters news agency reported that recurring power and water cuts were among the grievances raised at the October 17 demonstration.
paras.zh: 据路透社报道，10 月 17 日示威活动中引发的不满包括反复断电和断水。

paras.en: For small businesses, interruptions to basic services can mean lost customers and income. Where jobs are already scarce, such disruptions make earning a living even harder.
paras.zh: 对于小型企业来说，基本服务中断可能意味着失去客户和收入。在工作岗位本来就稀缺的地方，这种干扰使谋生变得更加困难。

paras.en: In L’Aouina, a northern suburb of Tunis, 20-year-old barber Khalil said he was waiting for an opportunity to leave the country by boat.
paras.zh: 在突尼斯北郊拉维纳，20 岁的理发师哈利勒说，他正在等待乘船离开该国的机会。

paras.en: “There’s nothing worth staying for in this country. Dying at sea would be a relief,” he said.
paras.zh: “没有什么值得留在这个国家的。死在海上也算是一种解脱，”他说。

paras.en: “I’m going to leave as soon as I can, and let them figure out the solutions on their own. Our generation has borne the brunt of all these crises, and nothing is left for us.”
paras.zh: “我会尽快离开，让他们自己想办法。我们这一代人在所有这些危机中首当其冲，什么也没有留给我们。”

paras.en: Others struggle to keep their business afloat.
paras.zh: 其他人则努力维持自己的业务。

paras.en: Khalil’s neighbour, a grocery shop owner who asked not to be named, said persistent problems with the water supply had become exhausting.
paras.zh: 卡里尔的邻居是一位不愿透露姓名的杂货店老板，他表示，持续存在的供水问题已经让人筋疲力尽。

paras.en: “I think the only solution is for someone to take over this shop. I cannot keep up with these crises any more,” he said.
paras.zh: “我认为唯一的解决办法就是有人接管这家店。我再也无法应对这些危机了，”他说。

paras.en: For Ghanmi, the years without work have brought more than financial hardship.
paras.zh: 对于甘米来说，没有工作的岁月带来的不仅仅是经济困难。

paras.en: “The wound on the body heals, but the wound in the mind and heart does not heal,” she said. “It really does not heal.”
paras.zh: “身体上的伤口愈合了，但思想和心灵上的伤口却没有愈合，”她说。 “确实无法痊愈。”

articles.title: UK police rule out probe into Palestine Action post by PM adviser’s wife

paras.en: Police in the United Kingdom have determined that a social media post by the wife of Prime Minister Andy Burnham’s national security adviser that appears to endorse Palestine Action, a group proscribed in the country as a “terrorist” organisation, does not merit a criminal investigation.
paras.zh: 英国警方已确定，首相安迪·伯纳姆的国家安全顾问的妻子在社交媒体上发表的一篇似乎支持“巴勒斯坦行动”的帖子不值得进行刑事调查，该组织在该国被列为“恐怖”组织。

paras.en: A Metropolitan Police spokesperson on Saturday said that officers looked at Sarah Helm’s post and ruled that it “did not meet the criminal threshold. No further police action will be taken.”
paras.zh: 伦敦警察厅发言人周六表示，警方查看了莎拉·赫尔姆的帖子，并裁定其“不符合刑事门槛。警方不会采取进一步行动。”

paras.en: The police had said on Friday that Helm’s post was “being assessed to determine whether any further police investigation may be required”.
paras.zh: 警方周五表示，正在对赫尔姆的帖子进行评估，以确定是否需要进行进一步的警方调查。

paras.en: Helm, an author and journalist who is married to National Security Adviser Jonathan Powell, wrote on X on Thursday: “God help us authors who support Palestine and Palestine Action.”
paras.zh: 赫尔姆是一位作家兼记者，国家安全顾问乔纳森·鲍威尔的丈夫，周四在 X 上写道：“上帝帮助我们支持巴勒斯坦和巴勒斯坦行动的作家。”

paras.en: Helm made the comment after publisher Faber said this week that its Irish author Sally Rooney could not sell her books in the UK, after she announced her plans to use the royalties to support Palestine Action.
paras.zh: 赫尔姆发表上述评论之前，出版商法贝尔本周表示，其爱尔兰作家莎莉·鲁尼（Sally Rooney）宣布计划使用版税支持巴勒斯坦行动后，无法在英国销售她的书。

paras.en: “Current legislation in the UK has led to circumstances where Faber cannot pass on UK earnings to Sally Rooney for her work. To sell a writer’s work and not be able to pass on earnings is an unconscionable situation for a publisher,” Faber said in a statement on its website.
paras.zh: “英国现行立法导致法贝尔无法将其在英国的收入转嫁给莎莉·鲁尼的作品。对于出版商来说，出售作家的作品而无法转交收入是一种不合理的情况，”法贝尔在其网站上的一份声明中表示。

paras.en: “As such, and in full agreement with Sally, we have taken the decision that we can no longer supply her works in the UK in any format,” the British publisher said, adding that it would continue to sell her work in other countries and regions.
paras.zh: 英国出版商表示：“因此，在与莎莉完全同意的情况下，我们决定不再以任何形式在英国供应她的作品。”并补充说，将继续在其他国家和地区销售她的作品。

paras.en: The Campaign Against Antisemitism, a British NGO, had responded on X that Helm’s post was “gobsmacking” and “clearly, the police need to investigate and Ms Helm must face the full force of the law”.
paras.zh: 英国非政府组织反犹太主义运动在 X 上回应称，赫尔姆的帖子“令人目瞪口呆”，“显然，警方需要调查，赫尔姆女士必须面对法律的全部制裁”。

paras.en: After being asked for comment on Friday, a government spokesperson said Helm’s comments did “not represent the government in any capacity”.
paras.zh: 周五被要求发表评论后，一名政府发言人表示，赫尔姆的评论“不代表政府的任何身份”。

paras.en: Palestine Action has been proscribed as a “terrorist” organisation since a July 2025 vote by UK lawmakers.
paras.zh: 自英国立法者于 2025 年 7 月投票以来，巴勒斯坦行动已被列为“恐怖”组织。

paras.en: Amnesty International says more than 3,500 people have been arrested in the UK for allegedly supporting Palestine Action since it was banned last year, many of them for holding up placards.
paras.zh: 国际特赦组织表示，自去年巴勒斯坦行动被禁止以来，已有超过 3,500 人因涉嫌支持巴勒斯坦行动而在英国被捕，其中许多人因举起标语牌而被捕。

paras.en: Palestine Action challenged the government’s decision to ban the group, but the Court of Appeal ruled in June that the proscription was lawful.
paras.zh: 巴勒斯坦行动组织对政府禁止该组织的决定提出质疑，但上诉法院 6 月裁定禁令合法。

articles.title: Scuffles and fires break out as protesters rally across France, joining students
articles.author: The Associated Press

paras.en: Scuffles and fires break out as protesters rally across France, joining students
paras.zh: 抗议者与学生一起在法国各地集会，发生扭打和火灾

paras.en: PARIS — A car and a newspaper kiosk were set on fire in Paris as police used tear gas and water cannons to disperse violent groups of protesters, while similar tensions erupted Saturday in other big cities on the fringes of nationwide demonstrations against rising living costs and in support of high school students' grievances.
paras.zh: 巴黎——警察使用催泪瓦斯和高压水枪驱散暴力抗议者，巴黎一辆汽车和一个报刊亭被纵火。周六，在全国范围内反对生活成本上涨和支持高中生申诉的示威活动边缘，其他大城市也爆发了类似的紧张局势。

paras.en: Interior Minister Laurent Nuñez's office described "a growing number of violent incidents," including assaults on police officers, looting or attempted looting of shops and damage to public buildings. Authorities reported at least 272 arrests across the country, including in Paris.
paras.zh: 内政部长洛朗·努涅斯的办公室描述了“越来越多的暴力事件”，包括袭击警察、抢劫或企图抢劫商店以及破坏公共建筑。当局报告称，包括巴黎在内的全国各地至少有 272 人被捕。

paras.en: In the French capital, police used tear gas and water cannons to push back people wearing hoods and masks and throwing fireworks and other objects at officers in the Place de la République, northeast of the Paris city center. Large numbers of riot police were deployed in the square and surrounding streets.
paras.zh: 在法国首都巴黎市中心东北部的共和广场，警方使用催泪瓦斯和高压水枪驱赶那些戴着头巾和面具并向警察投掷烟花和其他物体的人。广场及周边街道部署了大量防暴警察。

paras.en: The majority of peaceful protesters joined a march that moved toward northwestern Paris. The crowd chanted France's national anthem as French flags were waved. The chants were accompanied by people playing trumpets and violins.
paras.zh: 大多数和平抗议者参加了向巴黎西北部移动的游行。当法国国旗挥舞时，人群高喊法国国歌。人们吹着小号和小提琴伴奏着圣歌。

paras.en: Meanwhile, police were working to prevent other small groups of protesters from converging on government buildings, Nuñez's office said.
paras.zh: 与此同时，努涅斯办公室表示，警方正在努力阻止其他小股抗议者聚集在政府大楼前。

paras.en: Many metro stations were closed Saturday at police request, including those around the Champs-Elysées and near the presidential palace, parliament and government offices.
paras.zh: 许多地铁站周六应警方要求关闭，包括香榭丽舍大街周围以及总统府、议会和政府办公室附近的地铁站。

paras.en: Violence hit Lyon, Marseille and other cities
paras.zh: 里昂、马赛等城市发生暴力事件

paras.en: In Lyon, France's third-largest city, where about 20,000 protesters joined the march, fire broke out inside a tourist office. Smoke and flames were seen rising from the building.
paras.zh: 在法国第三大城市里昂，大约有两万名抗议者参加了游行，旅游局内发生火灾。看到烟雾和火焰从建筑物中升起。

paras.en: In the southern port city of Marseille, some shops and a municipal police station were damaged, while some protesters briefly forced their way into the lobby of City Hall.
paras.zh: 在南部港口城市马赛，一些商店和一个市警察局遭到破坏，一些抗议者短暂强行闯入市政厅大厅。

paras.en: "This is unacceptable," Marseille Mayor Benoît Payan told BFM TV, describing the damage in City Hall as "limited."
paras.zh: 马赛市长伯努瓦·帕扬 (Benoît Payan) 告诉 BFM 电视台：“这是不可接受的”，他称市政厅的损失“有限”。

paras.en: Nuñez's office also reported violence by masked groups in Rennes, Toulouse, Montpellier and Grenoble, among other cities.
paras.zh: 努涅斯办公室还报告了雷恩、图卢兹、蒙彼利埃和格勒诺布尔等城市蒙面团体的暴力事件。

paras.en: Protesters across France responded to calls on social media to revive the "yellow vest" movement, which emerged in 2018 against social injustice. Demonstrators expressed widespread frustration and anger at the government as gasoline, energy and food prices have spiked in recent months.
paras.zh: 法国各地的抗议者响应社交媒体上的呼吁，重振2018年兴起的反对社会不公正的“黄背心”运动。由于近几个月汽油、能源和食品价格飙升，示威者对政府表达了普遍的不满和愤怒。

paras.en: Saturday's protests follow weeks of school blockades
paras.zh: 周六的抗议活动是在学校封锁数周之后发生的

paras.en: Student groups protesting since mid-September through school blockades have urged supporters to join them.
paras.zh: 自九月中旬以来，学生团体通过封锁学校进行抗议，并敦促支持者加入他们的行列。

paras.en: The CGT, one of France's major labor unions, also backed the protests, calling for "higher wages and pensions, lower prices and the protection of public services that meet people's needs."
paras.zh: 法国主要工会之一的CGT也支持抗议活动，呼吁“提高工资和养老金、降低物价并保护满足人民需求的公共服务”。

paras.en: In recent weeks, France has seen thousands of arrests, hundreds of injuries and schools set on fire as the new school year descended into nationwide student protests that are influencing the country's presidential election campaign and drawing international attention.
paras.zh: 最近几周，随着新学年进入全国范围内的学生抗议活动，法国发生了数千人被捕、数百人受伤和学校被纵火的事件，这些抗议活动正在影响该国的总统竞选活动并引起国际关注。

paras.en: Among protesters, particularly gruesome wounds suffered by some teenagers have been blamed on police riot-control weapons. Nuñez suspended the use of a type of police stun grenade against the young demonstrators after a 15-year-old lost a hand.
paras.zh: 在抗议者中，一些青少年所受的严重伤害被归咎于警察的防暴武器。在一名 15 岁青少年失去一只手后，努涅斯暂停对年轻示威者使用一种警察眩晕手榴弹。

paras.en: On Tuesday, climate and social justice activist Greta Thunberg joined students at a high school in the Paris suburb of Saint-Denis.
paras.zh: 周二，气候和社会正义活动家格蕾塔·通伯格 (Greta Thunberg) 与巴黎郊区圣但尼一所高中的学生们一起。

articles.title: The state of the State Department in the wake of the Kimberly Guilfoyle scandal
articles.author: Joel Rose

paras.en: The state of the State Department in the wake of the Kimberly Guilfoyle scandal
paras.zh: 金伯利·吉尔福伊尔丑闻后国务院的状况

paras.en: NPR's Joel Rose talks with James B. Story, former U.S. Ambassador to Venezuela, about the state of the State Department in the wake of the Kimberly Guilfoyle scandal.
paras.zh: 美国国家公共广播电台 (NPR) 的乔尔·罗斯 (Joel Rose) 与美国前驻委内瑞拉大使詹姆斯·斯托里 (James B. Story) 讨论了金伯利·吉尔福伊尔 (Kimberly Guilfoyle) 丑闻后国务院的状况。

paras.en: The American ambassador to Greece resigned under pressure this week. Kimberly Guilfoyle, the ex-fiancee of President Trump's son, served in her role for about a year until a story by the Wall Street Journal reported that she'd asked a Trump donor to pay her credit card bill before she was appointed. This scandal is yet another blow for America's diplomatic corps, already understaffed during President Trump's second term.
paras.zh: 美国驻希腊大使本周迫于压力辞职。特朗普总统儿子的前未婚妻金伯利·吉尔福伊尔(Kimberly Guilfoyle)担任该职务大约一年，直到《华尔街日报》报道称，她在被任命之前要求特朗普的一位捐助者支付她的信用卡账单。这一丑闻对美国外交使团来说是又一次打击，在特朗普总统第二任期内，美国外交使团就已经人手不足。

paras.en: So what is the state of the U.S. State Department? We have called up James Story, a former U.S. ambassador to Venezuela and a state department veteran to answer that question. Ambassador, welcome to the program.
paras.zh: 那么美国国务院的状况如何呢？我们致电美国前驻委内瑞拉大使、国务院资深人士詹姆斯·斯托里来回答这个问题。大使，欢迎来到这个节目。

paras.en: JAMES STORY: Thank you all so much for having me today. Appreciate it.
paras.zh: 詹姆斯·斯托里：非常感谢大家今天邀请我参加。欣赏它。

paras.en: ROSE: I want to say first, NPR has not confirmed the reporting by the Wall Street Journal, but I wonder what your reaction was to Miss Guilfoyle's resignation.
paras.zh: 罗斯：我首先想说的是，美国公共广播电台尚未证实《华尔街日报》的报道，但我想知道您对吉尔福伊尔小姐的辞职有何反应。

paras.en: STORY: I was simply astonished. As a diplomat, anybody in the foreign service - and certainly as an ambassador - we're under extraordinary scrutiny on gifts you can accept. Anyone looking to do work with the U.S. government, you're prohibited from receiving gifts from them. So the fact that allegedly someone spent 100,000 - or there was a request for $100,000 to pay off a credit card bill - was really astonishing to me.
paras.zh: 故事：我只是感到惊讶。作为一名外交官，任何从事外交工作的人，当然还有大使，我们都会对您可以接受的礼物进行严格审查。任何想要与美国政府合作的人都被禁止接受他们的礼物。因此，据称有人花费了 100,000 美元——或者有人要求支付 100,000 美元来偿还信用卡账单——这一事实确实令我感到惊讶。

paras.en: ROSE: You were a career diplomat under administrations of both parties and retired this May. How do you assess the State Department as you have known it versus how it exists today?
paras.zh: 罗斯：您曾是两党政府的职业外交官，于今年五月退休。您如何评价您所熟知的国务院与现在的国务院？

paras.en: STORY: So I think the state of the State Department right now is in flux. We certainly lost a lot of really talented folks. The fact that we're out recruiting for new people right now is indicative of the fact that we don't have enough people doing America's diplomacy abroad. I mean, we are the first line of defense for the American people. And I think we need to be well-funded. The State Department needs to be well-funded. But again, certainly, you can always improve an organization. You can always do better as an organization. But I think some of the changes that transpired were ultimately very harmful to the State Department.
paras.zh: 故事：所以我认为国务院目前的状况正在不断变化。我们确实失去了很多真正有才华的人。我们现在正在招募新人，这一事实表明我们没有足够的人员来从事美国的海外外交工作。我的意思是，我们是美国人民的第一道防线。我认为我们需要充足的资金。国务院需要充足的资金。但同样，当然，你总是可以改进一个组织。作为一个组织，你总是可以做得更好。但我认为所发生的一些变化最终对国务院非常有害。

paras.en: ROSE: There are some very big events happening around the world at a time when the top job in some U.S. embassies around the world is vacant. And I'm thinking of Russia, of Ukraine, of Germany, and I could name many others. What's the impact on American foreign policy when so many of these positions are not staffed?
paras.zh: 罗斯：当美国驻世界各地大使馆的最高职位出现空缺时，世界各地正在发生一些非常重大的事件。我想到了俄罗斯、乌克兰、德国，我还可以举出许多其他国家的名字。当这么多职位空缺时，这对美国外交政策有何影响？

paras.en: STORY: Well, I can tell you, you know, the host government, first of all, views the lead diplomat from the United States differently if she or he is an ambassador, meaning the president's personal representative, or a charge d'affaires. The Saudi family, the kingdom, do not want to deal with a charge d'affaires. They want to have an ambassador, a seated ambassador. So you have a little more power when it comes to organizing the interagency. Your engagement directly with the government, I think, all comes down to having gone through that Senate confirmation process and being chosen, then going through all the scrutiny, financial and otherwise, that allows you to be abroad as an ambassador representing the United States. And when you don't have that, you're indicating at times to that country that, well, we're not prioritizing you.
paras.zh: 故事：嗯，我可以告诉你，你知道，首先，如果美国首席外交官是大使（即总统的个人代表或临时代办），东道国政府对她或他的看法有所不同。沙特家族、王国不想与代办打交道。他们想要一位大使，一位坐着的大使。因此，在组织跨机构方面，你拥有更多的权力。我认为，你与政府的直接接触，归根结底都在于经历了参议院的确认程序并被选中，然后经历了所有的审查、财务和其他方面的审查，这使你能够作为代表美国的大使出国。当你没有这样的能力时，你有时会向那个国家表明，我们不会优先考虑你。

paras.en: ROSE: What about not having ambassadors in many countries in the Middle East and the Persian Gulf? What is the concrete impact, would you say, of that?
paras.zh: 罗斯：在中东和波斯湾的许多国家都没有大使怎么办？您认为这有什么具体影响？

paras.en: STORY: The first impact is that you're losing out on tremendous experience. When you don't have that person, especially right now in the Middle East, I think it puts us fundamentally in a bad position. You have this war in Iran that is expanding. It affects all of the different countries in the region. It's definitely a regional conflict now. Who is the person that goes in, that gives the message - in Qatar or in Kuwait or Iraq or what have you - to that host country? And does that message have the same resonance that it would have if that person had been the ambassador? And I would say that it does not.
paras.zh: 故事：第一个影响是你失去了丰富的经验。当你没有那个人时，特别是现在在中东，我认为这从根本上使我们处于不利的境地。伊朗的战争正在扩大。它影响到该地区所有不同的国家。现在肯定是地区冲突了。谁是在卡塔尔、科威特、伊拉克或其他地方向东道国传达信息的人？如果这个人是大使，这个信息是否会产生同样的共鸣？我想说事实并非如此。

paras.en: ROSE: Just under 50% of U.S. ambassadorships are vacant. Is it unusual for a number to be that large so far into a president's term?
paras.zh: 罗斯：不到 50% 的美国大使职位空缺。总统任期内如此之多的数字是否不寻常？

paras.en: STORY: It's certainly unusual. And unfortunately, this has become a bipartisan problem of Senate nominations for judges and ambassadors and others to be held up based on other things. And it used to be kind of a regular process where people would go up, and you'd get red-lined out. In other words, basically, by unanimous consent, ambassadors were approved. Unless there were some big problems, it's pretty extreme right now to have so many ambassadorships empty.
paras.zh: 故事：这确实不寻常。不幸的是，这已经成为参议院对法官、大使和其他人的提名因其他原因而被搁置的两党问题。这曾经是一种常规流程，人们会上去，而你会被划出红线。换句话说，基本上是一致同意，大使才被批准的。除非出现什么大问题，否则现在这么多大使职位空缺是相当极端的。

paras.en: But it's even more extreme to have so many ambassadorships headed over to political appointees rather than people who have spent decades working in the foreign service, learning the language, learning the history, understanding the bilateral relationships, understanding how Washington works. And when you put amateurs - and some political appointees are good, let me be very clear. But when you put amateurs in charge, sometimes you'll get an amateur outcome.
paras.zh: 但更极端的是，这么多大使职位都交给了政治任命者，而不是那些在外交部门工作了几十年、学习语言、学习历史、了解双边关系、了解华盛顿如何运作的人。当你把业余人士——以及一些政治任命的人——都很好时，让我说得非常清楚。但当你让业余人士负责时，有时你会得到业余的结果。

paras.en: And I think in the case of Ambassador Guilfoyle in Greece, we had a very amateur outcome that was foretold based on all of the problems that should have come out in her vetting before being identified. What particular skills she brought to bear for Greece - other than proximity, perhaps - remained a question mark for us. But for me, it's the 80% of ambassadors that have actually been put in the field are political appointees - that's the most shocking statistic.
paras.zh: 我认为就驻希腊吉尔福伊尔大使而言，我们得到了一个非常业余的结果，这是基于她在确定之前审查中应该出现的所有问题而预测的。她为希腊带来了哪些特殊技能——也许除了邻近之外——对我们来说仍然是一个问号。但对我来说，实际派驻的大使中有 80% 是政治任命的——这是最令人震惊的统计数据。

paras.en: ROSE: Yeah, help me understand what's going on there because other administrations have political appointees in important ambassadorships, right? What's been different about how this administration is doing it?
paras.zh: 罗斯：是的，帮助我了解那里发生的事情，因为其他政府在重要的大使职位上都有政治任命的人，对吧？本届政府的做法有何不同？

paras.en: STORY: Well, now it's not just for certain bilateral missions where the expectations of the host country is that it's going to be somebody close to the president, right? The Court of St. James, for instance, for Great Britain - that always goes to a political appointee, somebody who can pick up the phone and get the president on the line.
paras.zh: 故事：嗯，现在不仅仅是某些双边任务，东道国期望它是与总统关系密切的人，对吧？例如，英国的圣詹姆斯法院——总是由政治任命者负责，这个人可以拿起电话让总统接通。

paras.en: And anywhere you have a bilateral relationship that's stable, then you have a few countries that sometimes are political appointees and sometimes are career people. Brazil is an example. Most of the time, it goes to a career person, not a political. What we're seeing now is that countries that have traditionally had hairier relationships, let's say, have gone political rather than to the traditional route. At some point, that inexperience may be seen.
paras.zh: 凡是双边关系稳定的地方，都会有一些国家有时是政治任命者，有时是职业人士。巴西就是一个例子。大多数时候，它是针对职业人士，而不是政治人士。我们现在看到的是，传统上关系比较复杂的国家已经走上了政治路线，而不是走传统路线。在某些时候，这种缺乏经验的情况可能会被发现。

paras.en: ROSE: The US Agency for International Development, generally known as USAID, ceased functioning as an independent entity in July, and the State Department took over some foreign assistance programs. How is that working, in your view?
paras.zh: 罗斯：美国国际开发署（通常称为 USAID）于 7 月停止作为独立实体运作，国务院接管了一些外国援助项目。您认为效果如何？

paras.en: STORY: Well, it's like asking somebody that shops at the grocery store for vegetables to become a farmer, to be honest with you. We had a competitive advantage against every other country in the world for how we did development. You know, we saved millions of lives through PEPFAR, a George Bush program - this was the President's Emergency Program For AIDS Relief - millions of lives saved in Africa providing HIV medications.
paras.zh: 故事：老实说，这就像要求在杂货店购买蔬菜的人成为农民一样。我们的发展方式比世界上所有其他国家都具有竞争优势。你知道，我们通过乔治·布什总统的总统紧急救援计划（PEPFAR）拯救了数百万人的生命——这是总统的艾滋病紧急救援计划——通过提供艾滋病毒药物拯救了非洲数百万人的生命。

paras.en: So you had people who spent 20 or 30 years who really understood how to do these programs, and now we're supposed to replicate that with people who have good intentions but don't have the experience. I think this is going to go down as one of the biggest own-goals we've ever had.
paras.zh: 因此，有些人花了 20 或 30 年的时间才真正了解如何实施这些项目，现在我们应该向那些有良好意愿但没有经验的人复制这一点。我认为这将成为我们有史以来最大的乌龙球之一。

paras.en: I think that USAID needed some reform. I don't disagree that it should have been housed within the State Department, for instance. I think, you know, sometimes we needed to have more policy control over some of the development programs we were doing. But to wholesale destroy an organization that had done so much goodwill and built up so much soft power for the United States, it really is something that - for me, it doesn't make a lot of sense.
paras.zh: 我认为美国国际开发署需要进行一些改革。例如，我不同意它应该设在国务院内。我认为，你知道，有时我们需要对我们正在进行的一些发展计划进行更多的政策控制。但要大规模摧毁一个为美国提供了如此多善意并建立了如此多软实力的组织，这对我来说确实没有多大意义。

paras.en: ROSE: I've been speaking to former U.S. ambassador James Story. Thank you very much for your time.
paras.zh: 罗斯：我一直在与美国前大使詹姆斯·斯托里交谈。非常感谢您抽出时间。

paras.en: STORY: Thank you so much for having me today.
paras.zh: 故事：非常感谢您今天邀请我。

paras.zh: NPR 文字记录的准确性和可用性可能有所不同。转录文本可能会被修改以纠正错误或匹配音频更新。 npr.org 上的音频可能会在其原始广播或发布后进行编辑。 NPR 节目的权威记录是音频记录。

articles.title: Student protests widen into greater social unrest in France
articles.author: Eleanor Beardsley

paras.en: Student protests widen into greater social unrest in France
paras.zh: 法国学生抗议活动扩大为更大的社会动荡

paras.en: Hundreds of protests took place in cities across France. Most of them were peaceful but some turned chaotic and violent.
paras.zh: 法国各地城市发生了数百起抗议活动。他们中的大多数是和平的，但也有一些变得混乱和暴力。

paras.en: Student-led demonstrations over education have broadened into wider social unrest in several European countries. In Albania today, police fired rubber bullets at young people protesting over rising living costs and a luxury development linked to Jared Kushner, President Trump's son-in-law. And in France, hundreds of protest marches have been taking place all across the country. Public sector workers and unions have now joined with the students who have been protesting for weeks. And while most of the demonstrations were peaceful, there were also scenes of chaos, violence and destruction in several cities. We go now to NPR's Eleanor Beardsley, who is out in Paris today, among the protesters. Thanks for joining us.
paras.zh: 在几个欧洲国家，学生主导的教育示威活动已扩大为更广泛的社会动荡。今天在阿尔巴尼亚，警察向抗议生活成本上涨和与特朗普总统女婿贾里德·库什纳有关的豪华开发项目的年轻人发射橡皮子弹。在法国，全国各地正在举行数百场抗议游行。公共部门工作人员和工会现已加入抗议数周的学生行列。尽管大多数示威活动都是和平的，但一些城市也出现了混乱、暴力和破坏的场面。现在我们请来 NPR 的埃莉诺·比尔兹利 (Eleanor Beardsley)，她今天出现在巴黎的抗议者中。感谢您加入我们。

paras.en: ELEANOR BEARDSLEY, BYLINE: You're welcome, Joel. Good to be with you.
paras.zh: 埃莉诺·比尔兹利连线：不客气，乔尔。很高兴和你在一起。

paras.en: ROSE: What was it like today? And was the feeling different than at other demonstrations?
paras.zh: 罗斯：今天怎么样？这种感觉与其他示威活动有什么不同吗？

paras.en: BEARDSLEY: Yeah, it really was. I would say France was like a split screen. So I was out amongst peaceful protesters, lots of students. Remember, it began with their demand for better resources, more teachers. They say their school buildings are dilapidated. But it's now been joined by a lot of public sector workers - firefighters, hospital workers, unions - angry over high prices, low wages and what they call general inequality. I spoke with 52-year-old social worker Julie Billat, who says she's especially angry over financial injustice. Here she is.
paras.zh: 比尔兹利：是的，确实如此。我想说法国就像一个分屏。所以我在和平抗议者中间，有很多学生。请记住，这始于他们对更好资源、更多教师的需求。他们说他们的校舍已经破旧不堪。但现在许多公共部门工作人员——消防员、医院工作人员、工会——也加入了这一行列，对高物价、低工资和他们所谓的普遍不平等感到愤怒。我与 52 岁的社会工作者 Julie Billat 进行了交谈，她说她对经济不公正感到特别愤怒。她在这里。

paras.en: JULIE BILLAT: We are. All the people who works - They don't earn much. They don't earn a lot of money, compared to some people who earn so much more. It's too much inequality.
paras.zh: 朱莉·比拉特：我们是。所有工作的人——他们挣得不多。与一些赚得多的人相比，他们赚的钱并不多。这实在是太不平等了。

paras.en: BEARDSLEY: And her friend, Anne Gauthier, chimes in to say that the police have treated the young people horribly. And there were horrible scenes of chaos and violence today.
paras.zh: 比尔兹利：她的朋友安妮·高蒂尔插话说，警察对待年轻人的方式很糟糕。今天出现了混乱和暴力的可怕场面。

paras.en: ROSE: Yeah, tell us more about that. What has been happening?
paras.zh: 罗斯：是的，请告诉我们更多相关信息。发生了什么事？

paras.en: UNIDENTIFIED COMMENTATOR: (Speaking French).
paras.zh: 身份不明的评论员：（法语）。

paras.en: BEARDSLEY: Well, you know, if you watch news channels like this one, BFM TV, it's just showing live all the violence all over France. In Paris, there's video of people setting fire to cars, huge bike stands, trash cans. There's black smoke billowing not far from the Eiffel Tower. Store windows have been smashed. There's pillaging going on. Young hooded youths broke into the town halls in Lille and Marseille. And in Marseille, we saw footage of them using metal street barricades as a battering ram to break into this ornate city hall. And inside, they threw to the ground a marble bust of Marianne. That is the symbol of the French Republic.
paras.zh: 比尔兹利：嗯，你知道，如果你观看像 BFM TV 这样的新闻频道，它会现场直播法国各地的所有暴力事件。在巴黎，有一段视频显示人们放火焚烧汽车、巨大的自行车停放处和垃圾桶。距离埃菲尔铁塔不远，黑烟滚滚。商店橱窗被砸碎。那里正在进行掠夺。年轻的蒙面青年闯入里尔和马赛的市政厅。在马赛，我们看到他们使用金属街道路障作为攻城锤闯入这座华丽的市政厅的镜头。在里面，他们把玛丽安的大理石半身像扔到了地上。这是法兰西共和国的象征。

paras.en: ROSE: Wow. What are people you talk to saying about all of this violence?
paras.zh: 罗斯：哇。与您交谈的人对所有这些暴力有何看法？

paras.en: BEARDSLEY: Well, this is a huge uptick. We haven't seen it like this in this movement, and students speaking on TV tonight are condemning it and begging authorities and the public not to let this overshadow what they say are their legitimate demands. And they also say TVs only show the worst cause that gets ratings. But a lot of people also say it's the police that have set the tone for this because they've been extremely aggressive with the young people, using tear gas and charging them. And that's what Elliott Seigneur, a 21-year-old who I spoke with today, told me. Here he is.
paras.zh: 比尔兹利：嗯，这是一个巨大的上升。我们在这场运动中还没有看到这样的情况，今晚在电视上发言的学生们对此表示谴责，并恳求当局和公众不要让这掩盖了他们所说的合法​​要求。他们还说电视只展示收视率最糟糕的原因。但很多人也表示，是警察为这件事定下了基调，因为他们对年轻人非常咄咄逼人，使用催泪瓦斯并指控他们。这就是我今天采访的 21 岁的 Elliott Seigneur 告诉我的。他在这里。

paras.en: ELLIOT SEIGNEUR: They gas us. They charge us with, like, literal military weapons. It's actually forbidden to have any type of equipment that is used to protect ourselves to - from the gas, from the charge and stuff like that. So necessarily, violence will break out.
paras.zh: ELLIOT SEIGNEUR： 他们给我们毒气。他们用真正的军事武器向我们冲锋。事实上，禁止拥有任何类型的用于保护我们自己的设备——免受毒气、电荷等的侵害。因此，暴力必然会爆发。

paras.en: ROSE: Eleanor, these protests have been going on for a month. How are they impacting France's presidential election, which is now less than six months away?
paras.zh: 罗斯：埃莉诺，这些抗议活动已经持续了一个月了。它们对距离现在还有不到六个月的法国总统选举有何影响？

paras.en: BEARDSLEY: The prime minister blamed what he called extreme violence on radical far-left groups. The far-left France Unbowed Party - whose firebrand leader, Jean-Luc Melenchon, is running for president - blames the police and the government. The far-right party of Marine Le Pen blames a breakdown in order. She's calling for more police, tougher penalties for young lawbreakers. She blames the far left for using the protesters, and it's true far-left politicians marched with the young people today.
paras.zh: 比尔兹利：首相将他所谓的极端暴力归咎于激进的极左团体。极左翼的法国不屈党——其煽动性领导人让-吕克·梅朗雄正在竞选总统——指责警察和政府。马琳·勒庞的极右翼政党指责秩序崩溃。她呼吁增加警察，对年轻违法者进行更严厉的惩罚。她指责极左派利用抗议者，而今天极左派政客确实与年轻人一起游行。

paras.en: Both parties blame President Emmanuel Macron, which is easy because he's been in charge for the last 10 years. They say he's made the country much worse. Analysts say he has lost the French youth today. One commentator said there's a complete political fracture in France, and today has surely deepened that divide.
paras.zh: 两党都指责总统埃马纽埃尔·马克龙(Emmanuel Macron)，这很容易，因为他在过去十年里一直执政。他们说他让这个国家变得更糟。分析人士称，他今天失去了法国年轻人。一位评论员表示，法国政治上存在彻底的分裂，而今天无疑加深了这种分歧。

paras.en: ROSE: That is NPR's Eleanor Beardsley joining us from Paris. Eleanor, thank you very much.
paras.zh: 罗斯： NPR 的埃莉诺·比尔兹利 (Eleanor Beardsley) 从巴黎加入我们。埃莉诺，非常感谢你。

paras.en: Accuracy and availability of NPR transcripts may vary. Transcript text may be revised to correct errors or match updates to audio. Audio on npr.org may be edited after its original broadcast or publication. The authoritative record of NPR’s programming is the audio record.
paras.zh: NPR 文字记录的准确性和可用性可能有所不同。转录文本可能会被修改以纠正错误或匹配音频更新。 npr.org 上的音频可能会在其原始广播或发布后进行编辑。 NPR 节目的权威记录是音频记录。

articles.title: Florida State falls again as Miami survives double-overtime scare to stay unbeaten

paras.en: Florida State has sputtered this season and Miami has not lost a game. Both trends held true, although barely, as the Hurricanes needed two overtimes to survive another upset bid on a day filled with chaotic finishes and upsets.
paras.zh: 佛罗里达州队本赛季表现不佳，而迈阿密队则没有输过一场比赛。这两种趋势都是正确的，尽管几乎没有，因为飓风队需要两个加时才能在充满混乱的结局和不安的一天中度过另一场令人沮丧的比赛。

paras.en: Miami quarterback Darian Mensah threw for 326 yards and three touchdowns, the last of them a 3-yarder to Malachi Toney in the second overtime, and No. 3 Miami held on to beat archrival FSU 43-35 in a back-and-forth classic.
paras.zh: 迈阿密四分卫达里安·门萨 (Darian Mensah) 传出 326 码并取得 3 次达阵，其中最后一次达阵是在第二个加时赛中给马拉奇·托尼 (Malachi Toney) 的 3 码达阵，而排名第三的迈阿密队以 43-35 击败了宿敌 FSU，打出了一场来回经典的比赛。

paras.en: Toney finished the night with 154 receiving yards and threw a 2-point conversion pass to Cooper Barkate. Hurricanes defensive back Bryce Fitzgerald sealed the win with an interception for the Hurricanes on the final play.
paras.zh: 托尼以 154 码的接球码数结束了当晚的比赛，并向库珀·巴卡特 (Cooper Barkate) 传出两分转换传球。飓风队防守后卫布莱斯·菲茨杰拉德在最后一场比赛中通过拦截为飓风队锁定了胜利。

paras.en: Ashton Daniels threw for 298 yards and four touchdowns for FSU. Duce Robinson had a pair of touchdown catches late, including a 75-yarder that tied the game with less than three minutes left in regulation and a 20-yard score to open the first overtime.
paras.zh: 阿什顿·丹尼尔斯 (Ashton Daniels) 为 FSU 传球 298 码并达阵 4 次。杜斯·罗宾逊在最后时刻完成了两次达阵，其中包括在常规时间还剩不到三分钟时的一记 75 码达阵，以及拉开第一个加时赛序幕的 20 码得分。

paras.en: Florida State head coach Mike Norvell has faced endless speculation about his job security, having been at the helm of a team that's had one of the nation’s worst records over the last three years.
paras.zh: 佛罗里达州立大学主教练迈克·诺维尔（Mike Norvell）面临着关于他的工作保障的无休止的猜测，他所执教的球队是过去三年来全美战绩最差的球队之一。

paras.en: Starting with the 2023 Orange Bowl debacle against Georgia, the Seminoles have now lost 14 consecutive games away from Tallahassee and are 0-13 since 2017 in true road games against ranked teams.
paras.zh: 自 2023 年橙色碗比赛惨败于佐治亚州以来，塞米诺尔队在客场对阵塔拉哈西队的比赛中已连续输掉 14 场比赛，并且自 2017 年以来在与排名球队的真正客场比赛中战绩为 0 胜 13 负。

paras.en: The Associated Press contributed to this report.
paras.zh: 美联社对此报道作出了贡献。

articles.title: Rays even ALCS at two games apiece with Game 4 win over Guardians after series postponement

paras.en: It will take at least six games to crown an American League champion.
paras.zh: 至少需要六场比赛才能加冕美国联盟冠军。

paras.en: The Tampa Bay Rays tied the ALCS at two games apiece, winning Game 4 over the Cleveland Guardians 7-3.
paras.zh: 坦帕湾光芒队与 ALCS 各打两场平局，在第四场比赛中以 7-3 战胜克利夫兰卫队。

paras.en: The Guardians got on the board early, as Chase DeLauter drove in Steven Kwan with an RBI single in the first. But Cleveland's offense was quiet after that.
paras.zh: 守护者队很早就加入了董事会，蔡斯·德劳特(Chase DeLauter)在第一场比赛中就打出了一记打点单打，击败了史蒂文·关(Steven Kwan)。但此后克利夫兰的进攻陷入平静。

paras.en: Tampa Bay got the run back with a two-out rally in the third — Yandy Diaz doubled, and then Jonathan Aranda drove him in to tie the game. In the sixth inning, Junior Caminero smoked an RBI double with runners on first and second and none out to give the Rays a 2-1 lead, but they squandered an opportunity to tack on more.
paras.zh: 坦帕湾队在第三局中以二出局的比分反超比分——扬迪·迪亚兹（Yandy Diaz）双打，然后乔纳森·阿兰达（Jonathan Aranda）将他带入，将比赛扳平。第六局，朱尼奥·卡米内罗打出打点双打，第一、第二跑垒员无人出局，让光芒队以 2-1 领先，但他们浪费了进一步进攻的机会。

paras.en: The Rays began the next frame with runners on second and third, no outs and the top of their order at the plate. Diaz struck out, but Aranda brought both of the runs in to give Tampa Bay a 4-1 lead. He would score on a sac fly two batters later.
paras.zh: 光线队以第二和第三名的跑者开始下一局，没有出局，并且在本垒上排名最高。迪亚兹三振出局，但阿兰达将两分都打进，坦帕湾队以 4-1 领先。两个击球手之后，他将通过袋飞得分。

paras.en: Cleveland was able to cut the deficit in half in the bottom half of the frame and even got the lead run to the plate but couldn't take full advantage. In the top of the ninth, Diaz added some huge insurance runs with a two-out, two-run jack that DeLauter just missed robbing.
paras.zh: 克利夫兰在下半场将比分差距缩小了一半，甚至在本垒上取得了领先，但未能充分利用优势。在第九局上半，迪亚兹用一个两出两分的杰克增加了一些巨大的保险跑动，德劳特刚刚错过了抢劫。

paras.en: Any lead is comfortable for All-Star closer Bryan Baker, but four runs was a walk in the park. He got a double play after a leadoff single, and he struck out Angel Martinez to end the game.
paras.zh: 对于全明星终结者布莱恩·贝克来说，任何领先优势都很舒服，但四分跑却是在公园里散步。他在首场单打后获得了双打，并三振了安吉尔·马丁内斯结束了比赛。

paras.en: No team has won back-to-back games this series.
paras.zh: 本系列赛没有球队连续赢球。

paras.en: The series was postponed due to weather on Friday night, pushing both Games 4 and 5 back one day each. Game 6 will be played on Monday as normally scheduled, but there are no more scheduled off days this series.
paras.zh: 由于周五晚上的天气原因，该系列赛被推迟，第四场和第五场比赛各推迟一天。第六场比赛将照常在周一进行，但本系列赛不再安排休息日。

articles.title: College football faces another clock controversy after BYU upsets Notre Dame

paras.en: It was a wild Saturday in college football, and if top team after top team taking losses wasn’t crazy enough, another game ended with a one-second clock controversy.
paras.zh: 对于大学橄榄球来说，这是一个疯狂的周六，如果顶级球队接连输球还不够疯狂，那么另一场比赛就会以一秒钟的争议结束。

paras.en: BYU pulled off an upset over Notre Dame — but social media seems to think the game may not have actually been over.
paras.zh: 杨百翰大学击败了圣母大学，但社交媒体似乎认为比赛可能还没有真正结束。

paras.en: Thanks to the No. 1 Georgia Bulldogs losing at home to Auburn, No. 2 Notre Dame had a chance to take over the top spot with a win.
paras.zh: 由于排名第一的佐治亚斗牛犬队在主场输给了奥本队，排名第二的圣母大学有机会以一场胜利取代榜首。

paras.en: Unfortunately, they would have to do that on the road against the Big 12's top team, the unbeaten No. 8 BYU Cougars.
paras.zh: 不幸的是，他们必须在客场对阵 Big 12 的顶级球队、不败的排名第八的杨百翰大学美洲狮队 (BYU Cougars) 时做到这一点。

paras.en: And, to make matters worse, the Fighting Irish were without one of their best defensive players almost immediately.
paras.zh: 而且，更糟糕的是，战斗爱尔兰队几乎立即失去了他们最好的防守球员之一。

paras.en: On BYU's first series, defensive lineman Boubacar Traore was called for targeting on a hit on BYU quarterback Bear Bachmeier.
paras.zh: 在杨百翰大学的第一个系列赛中，防守前锋布巴卡尔·特拉奥雷（Boubacar Traore）被要求瞄准杨百翰大学四分卫贝尔·巴赫迈尔（Bear Bachmeier）的一击。

paras.en: That was a costly penalty for a team that doesn't take a lot of them, and the Cougars made them pay.
paras.zh: 对于一支没有太多球员的球队来说，这是一个代价高昂的处罚，而美洲狮队让他们付出了代价。

paras.en: They marched downfield — even forcing Notre Dame to burn a timeout — with Bachmeier finding the end zone to open the scoring.
paras.zh: 他们向前推进，甚至迫使圣母大学暂停，巴赫迈尔找到了达阵区，首开纪录。

paras.en: Notre Dame hit a field goal in the first quarter and then found the end zone in the second with running back Nolan James Jr. hitting paydirt to give them a 10-7 lead.
paras.zh: 圣母大学在第一节命中一记投篮，然后在第二节跑卫小诺兰·詹姆斯 (Nolan James Jr.) 命中达阵，以 10-7 领先。

paras.en: However, BYU had more, particularly a trick play that saw Bachmeier trotting into the end zone with the help of a blocker.
paras.zh: 然而，杨百翰大学还有更多，特别是巴赫迈尔在拦网手的帮助下小跑进入达阵区的技巧。

paras.en: Then, as if that wasn't enough, Bachmeier scored another touchdown using his legs just before the half, and with the extra point, that gave BYU a 21-10 lead.
paras.zh: 然后，似乎这还不够，巴赫迈尔在上半场前再次用腿触地得分，凭借额外的一分，杨百翰大学以 21-10 领先。

paras.en: However, there was still enough time for Notre Dame to get another possession, and with just nine seconds on the clock, the Fighting Irish found themselves on the BYU 5-yard line.
paras.zh: 然而，圣母大学仍然有足够的时间再次控球，在比赛还剩九秒时，爱尔兰战斗队发现自己已经站在了杨百翰大学的 5 码线上。

paras.en: Notre Dame QB CJ Carr attempted to spike the ball, but he never had total control of it, and upon review, it was ruled a fumble, with the Irish leaving points on the table and forking over possession.
paras.zh: 圣母大学四分卫 CJ 卡尔试图扣球，但他从未完全控制住球，经过审查，结果被判定为掉球，爱尔兰队在积分榜上留下了分数，并放弃了控球权。

paras.en: Notre Dame battled back in the second half, and eventually found themselves up by a field goal.
paras.zh: 圣母大学在下半场奋力反击，最终凭借一记射门扳回一城。

paras.en: BYU responded when Bachmeier — who had already shown he can find the end zone as a rusher and receiver — threw his first passing touchdown of the game by finding tight end Walker Lyons with just under two minutes left in regulation.
paras.zh: 当巴赫迈尔（Bachmeier）做出回应时，巴赫迈尔（Bachmeier）已经证明了他可以作为冲球手和接球手找到端区，他在比赛还剩不到两分钟时找到近端锋沃克·莱昂斯（Walker Lyons），完成了比赛的第一次传球达阵。

paras.en: That gave BYU a four-point lead and meant Notre Dame couldn't settle for a field goal.
paras.zh: 这让杨百翰大学领先四分，意味着圣母大学不能满足于射门得分。

paras.en: The Irish converted on a crucial fourth-and-2 to keep their drive alive, but after failing to get into the end zone, they found themselves facing fourth-and-five with ten seconds remaining. They managed to convert with four seconds on the clock, setting up the final play of the game.
paras.zh: 爱尔兰队在关键的第四个和第二个位置上进行了转换，以保持他们的动力，但在未能进入达阵区后，他们发现自己在比赛还剩十秒时面临着第四个和第五个位置。他们在比赛还剩四秒时成功扳平比分，奠定了比赛的最终胜局。

paras.en: There was some contact on that one, but no flags. That'll frustrate Notre Dame fans, but not as much as this will.
paras.zh: 那里有一些接触，但没有旗帜。这会让巴黎圣母院的球迷感到沮丧，但不会那么沮丧。

paras.en: The field had been stormed, and both teams had headed to the locker room before that started making the rounds on social media.
paras.zh: 球场上一片混乱，两支球队都前往更衣室，然后开始在社交媒体上流传。

paras.en: That ended Notre Dame's 16-game winning streak and is one of several outcomes that are going to shake up the rankings and CFP picture in a big, big way.
paras.zh: 这结束了圣母大学的 16 连胜，也是将极大地改变排名和 CFP 形象的几个结果之一。

paras.en: Notre Dame will take a week off and then get back at it against Navy, while the Cougars will keep chugging along with a visit to Orlando to take on the UCF Knights.
paras.zh: 圣母大学将休息一周，然后在对阵海军的比赛中恢复比赛，而美洲狮队将继续前往奥兰多迎战 UCF 骑士队。

articles.title: Is sisterhood the secret to a long life? The Sardinian village that could hold key to women’s longevity
articles.author: Angela Giuffrida in Bolotana

paras.en: When Giovanna Marras opens the door to her home in Bolotana, a mountain village in central Sardinia, her eyes are bright with curiosity as she sizes up her visitors. Her sister, Mariangela, peeks out too, soon ushering her guests inside and handing out dishes of ice-cream. The sisters are full of life, talking animatedly. Giovanna is 101 and Mariangela is 99.
paras.zh: 当乔凡娜·马拉斯（Giovanna Marras）打开位于撒丁岛中部山村博洛塔纳（Bolotana）的家门时，她的眼睛里充满好奇，打量着来访者。她的妹妹玛丽安吉拉（Mariangela）也向外张望，很快就把她的客人引入室内，并分发了冰淇淋。姐妹俩精神饱满，谈笑风生。乔凡娜 101 岁，玛丽安吉拉 99 岁。

paras.en: Sitting in their living room, Giovanna swiftly recaps her life story: she excelled at school before moving to Cagliari, the capital of the Italian island, at 18 to train as a seamstress. The sisters went on to run a successful tailoring business in Bolotana before travelling the world after retirement. Neither married.
paras.zh: 坐在客厅里，乔凡娜迅速回顾了自己的人生故事：她在学校表现出色，18 岁时搬到意大利岛屿首府卡利亚里接受裁缝培训。姐妹俩在退休后环游世界之前，继续在博洛塔纳经营一家成功的裁缝店。都没有结婚。

paras.en: “Someone did come to the house and ask my parents for my hand in marriage,” Giovanna said. “I told them to tell him to go away – I mean, a woman should at least know her future husband.” Mariangela is equally as feisty in her response. “I didn’t want to get married … I walk my own path, I don’t need support.”
paras.zh: “确实有人​​来到我家向我父母求婚，”乔凡娜说。 “我告诉他们让他走开——我的意思是，一个女人至少应该了解她未来的丈夫。”马里安吉拉的回应也同样活跃。 “我不想结婚……我走自己的路，不需要支持。”

paras.en: The details of their lives are now being examined as part of a broader pattern of exceptional longevity in Bolotana, where women are driving a trend that could put the village, population 2,266, in the running to be the world’s sixth “blue zone” – geographic areas with unusually high concentrations of centenarians. Sardinia was home to the first such zone, identified more than 25 years ago.
paras.zh: 他们的生活细节现在正在接受审查，作为博洛塔纳超长寿命的更广泛模式的一部分，在那里，女性正在推动一种趋势，使这个人口为 2,266 人的村庄有望成为世界上第六个“蓝色区域”——百岁老人异常集中的地理区域。撒丁岛是第一个此类区域的所在地，该区域于 25 年前被发现。

paras.en: A study by professors at the University of Sassari and the University of Alabama at Birmingham in the US, published in the scientific journal Frontiers in Aging last week, found that 13.8% of women in Bolotana who reach the age of 70 will live to 100 – placing it second in the world for female longevity after Hong Kong.
paras.zh: 美国萨萨里大学和阿拉巴马大学伯明翰分校的教授上周在科学杂志《老龄化前沿》上发表的一项研究发现，博洛塔纳70岁以上的女性中有13.8%能活到100岁，在女性寿命方面位居世界第二，仅次于香港。

paras.en: Giovanna is the third eldest of six female centenarians in Bolotana, after Tonia Giglio and Maddalena Falchi, both 102. By the end of this year, two other women are expected to reach the milestone, and in 2027 two more, including Mariangela. The last male centenarian, Giovanni Madau, died in July, a few months short of his 102nd birthday.
paras.zh: 乔凡娜 (Giovanna) 是博洛塔纳 (Bolotana) 六位女性百岁老人中的第三位，仅次于托尼娅·吉利奥 (Tonia Giglio) 和马达莱娜·法尔奇 (Maddalena Falchi)，她们都是 102 岁。预计到今年年底，另外两名女性将达到这一里程碑，到 2027 年，另外两名女性将达到这一里程碑，其中包括玛丽安吉拉 (Mariangela)。最后一位男性百岁老人乔瓦尼·马杜 (Giovanni Madau) 于 7 月去世，距离他的 102 岁生日还有几个月。

paras.en: Tore Pedde, the president of Orminas, a cultural association, played a crucial role in uncovering Bolotana as a potential longevity hotspot after painstakingly searching its demographic archives, even tracking down centenarians born in the village who had long since moved overseas.
paras.zh: 文化协会奥尔米纳斯 (Orminas) 的主席托雷·佩德 (Tore Pedde) 在发现博洛塔纳作为潜在长寿热点的过程中发挥了关键作用，他煞费苦心地搜索了博洛塔纳的人口档案，甚至追踪到了出生在该村但早已移居海外的百岁老人。

paras.en: Records of people born in Bolotana between 1900 and 1925 showed that 38 had lived beyond 100, putting their longevity rate at 57% higher than the Italian national average.
paras.zh: 1900年至1925年间出生于博洛塔纳的人的记录显示，有38人活过100岁，他们的寿命比意大利全国平均水平高出57%。

paras.en: “Up until the early 1900s, Bolotana followed a trend whereby men significantly outnumbered women among the elderly,” Pedde said. “From the early 20th century onwards, however, the trend shifted and women began to outnumber men. Later, the number of female centenarians started to far exceed the male ones, and this trend continues today.”
paras.zh: “直到 1900 年代初，博洛塔纳一直遵循这样的趋势：老年人中男性数量明显多于女性，”佩德说。 “然而，从20世纪初开始，趋势发生了转变，女性的数量开始超过男性。后来，女性百岁老人的数量开始远远超过男性，这种趋势一直持续到今天。”

paras.en: While it has already been well established that women live longer for biological reasons, scientists behind the study are tracing family trees in search of genetic clues to Bolotana’s female longevity. They are also exploring the roles of diet, physical activity and social connections.
paras.zh: 虽然众所周知，女性寿命更长是出于生物学原因，但这项研究背后的科学家们正在追踪家谱，寻找博洛塔纳女性长寿的遗传线索。他们还在探索饮食、身体活动和社会联系的作用。

paras.en: A striking characteristic of Bolotana’s female centenarians is their independence. The Marras sisters still cook for themselves, eating a varied but clean diet without forsaking meat, cheese or wine. Mariangela does the shopping, which entails a walk down a hilly street and back.
paras.zh: 博洛塔纳女性百岁老人的一个显着特征是她们的独立。马拉斯姐妹仍然自己做饭，饮食多样但干净，不放弃肉类、奶酪或葡萄酒。 Mariangela 负责购物，需要沿着山路步行然后返回。

paras.en: The women have grit and are remarkably lucid. Filomena Scarpa, a former language teacher who turned 100 in January, began learning German in her 90s and was a voracious reader before a problem with her left eye started to hinder her. “It saddens me not to be able to read with the same level of consistency,” she said. She goes to a personal trainer twice a week. “Because I can’t sit around all day.”
paras.zh: 这些女性有勇气而且非常清醒。菲洛梅娜·斯卡帕 (Filomena Scarpa) 曾是一名语言教师，今年 1 月就迎来了 100 岁生日，她在 90 多岁时开始学习德语，在左眼问题开始困扰她之前，她一直是一位如饥似渴的读者。 “无法以同样程度的一致性阅读让我感到难过，”她说。她每周去看两次私人教练。 “因为我不能整天坐着。”

paras.en: Scarpa, who has two sons, is a childhood friend of Falchi, who now lives with her daughter about an hour away in Oristana. The pair speak often. Falchi is notorious in Bolotana for smoking like a trooper. “I told her to quit because it’s not good for her health,” Scarpa said. “But she said: ‘It hasn’t got me so far, so I shall carry on.’”
paras.zh: 斯卡帕有两个儿子，是法尔奇儿时的朋友，法尔奇现在和女儿住在距奥里斯塔纳约一小时车程的地方。两人经常说话。法尔奇在博洛塔纳因像士兵一样抽烟而臭名昭著。 “我告诉她戒烟，因为这对她的健康不利，”斯卡帕说。 “但她说：‘到目前为止，我还没有做到这一点，所以我会继续下去。’”

paras.en: Bolotana is situated in Sardinia’s Marghine mountains, about 70 miles (110km) from the island’s original blue zone – a cluster of villages nestled on the slopes of the central and eastern provinces.
paras.zh: 博洛塔纳位于撒丁岛的马吉尼山脉，距离岛上最初的蓝色区域（坐落在中部和东部省份山坡上的村庄群）约 70 英里（110 公里）。

paras.en: “What’s special here is that for the first time we’ve identified an area where women live to a great age, whereas the original blue zone was predominantly male,” said Giovanni Mario Pes, who led the study and is a co-creator of the blue zone concept. “We therefore need to explain why longevity specifically affects women here.”
paras.zh: “这里的特别之处在于，我们第一次确定了一个女性寿命较长的区域，而最初的蓝色区域主要是男性，”领导这项研究、蓝色区域概念的联合创始人乔瓦尼·马里奥·佩斯 (Giovanni Mario Pes) 说。 “因此，我们需要解释为什么长寿特别影响这里的女性。”

paras.en: Unlike the original villages, Bolotana is relatively close to cities, including Sassari and Alghero on the west coast. Still, its streets are steep, providing residents with unavoidable exercise. The environment is unspoiled and most people still eat fruit and vegetables grown in their gardens.
paras.zh: 与原来的村庄不同，博洛塔纳相对靠近城市，包括西海岸的萨萨里和阿尔盖罗。尽管如此，它的街道还是很陡峭，为居民提供了不可避免的锻炼机会。环境未受破坏，大多数人仍然吃自家花园种植的水果和蔬菜。

paras.en: One thing Pes noted among its female residents was a “strong sense of sisterhood”. “This felt quite unusual and is something I’d like to explore scientifically,” he added.
paras.zh: 佩斯在女性居民中注意到的一件事是“强烈的姐妹情谊”。 “这感觉很不寻常，是我想进行科学探索的事情，”他补充道。

paras.en: Francesco Manconi, the mayor of Bolotana, believes the sociality is key. “There is an abundance of natural affection, whether from family members, neighbours or friends, towards our elderly,” he said, adding that the village placed “a great importance” on ensuring they could stay in their own homes.
paras.zh: 博洛塔纳市市长弗朗西斯科·曼科尼 (Francesco Manconi) 认为，社交性是关键。他说：“无论是来自家人、邻居还是朋友，我们的老人都怀有丰富的自然感情。”他补充说，村里“非常重视”确保他们能够留在自己的家中。

paras.en: Betti Uda, who runs a tourism business, said the village’s elderly women were determined and still tried to live purposefully. “If they want to do something, they will – nothing holds them back.”
paras.zh: 经营旅游业的贝蒂·乌达 (Betti Uda) 表示，村里的老年妇女意志坚定，仍然努力有目标地生活。 “如果他们想做某事，他们就会去做——没有什么能阻止他们。”

articles.title: ‘4,000 people minding our own business’: four decades on, Falklands again face a hostile Argentina
articles.author: Daniel Boffey in Port Stanley, Falkland Islands; photographs and video by Sean Smith

paras.en: A dozen local people and a uniformed military police officer (“Do you mind if I sit in?”) took their seats at the back of the handsome wood-panelled courtroom that doubles as the Falkland Islands’ legislative assembly. Outside, it was a typically blowy early evening. It may nominally be spring in the south Atlantic, but Stanley harbour, with its dark grey water speckled with historical shipwrecks, was a cauldron of swells and churn.
paras.zh: 十几名当地人和一名身穿制服的宪兵（“你介意我坐在里面吗？”）在漂亮的木板法庭后面就座，法庭同时也是福克兰群岛的立法议会。外面是一个典型的傍晚时分，风很大。南大西洋名义上可能是春天，但斯坦利港的深灰色海水中点缀着历史上的沉船残骸，是一个汹涌澎湃的大锅。

paras.en: Six of the assembly’s eight members – five men, one woman – waited patiently at a row of desks and microphones. The heating had been turned up to just short of uncomfortable. Behind them, a portrait of King Charles. From the other walls, dusty photographs of governors, of varying popularity, gazed disinterestedly at the scene.
paras.zh: 议会八名成员中的六名——五男一女——在一排桌子和麦克风前耐心等待。暖气开到了让人不舒服的程度。他们身后是查尔斯国王的肖像。另一面墙上挂着满是灰尘的州长照片，这些照片的受欢迎程度各不相同，冷漠地注视着这一场景。

paras.en: Proceedings started at the raised hand of a bored-looking young man wearing headphones in the corner. He was transmitting the question and answer session via radio across the dozen or so inhabited islands that make up the 778-strong archipelago.
paras.zh: 会议开始于角落里一个戴着耳机、一脸无聊的年轻人举起的手。他通过无线电在十几个有人居住的岛屿上传送问答环节，这些岛屿由 778 个群岛组成。

paras.en: It was not clear how many of the Falklands’ 3,600 residents were listening in from their farm houses out in the diddle-dee shrub that coats much of the islands, or in the front rooms of Port Stanley’s white clapboard cottages with the pretty coloured roofs; likely not on a par with the number who learned 44 years ago from the Falkland Islands broadcasting station that their lands had been invaded.
paras.zh: 目前尚不清楚福克兰群岛的 3,600 名居民中，有多少人是在农舍里听声音，这些农舍的大部分岛屿都覆盖着迪德尔迪灌木丛，或者是在斯坦利港的白色隔板小屋和漂亮的彩色屋顶的前屋里听声音。可能与 44 年前从福克兰群岛广播电台得知自己的土地遭到入侵的人数不相上下。

paras.en: “There’s no turning back, we can expect them by dawn,” the governor, Rex Hunt, had said then.
paras.zh: “没有回头路了，我们可以在黎明前等待他们，”州长雷克斯·亨特当时说道。

paras.en: But for those who did tune in on Monday evening, there was much to dwell on. Not so much the answers about the local internet contract or the consultation on the contentious plan for a salmon farm.
paras.zh: 但对于那些周一晚上收听节目的人来说，还有很多值得思考的事情。与其说是关于当地互联网合同的答案，不如说是对有争议的鲑鱼养殖场计划的咨询。

paras.en: “I have another one for you,” piped up one enthusiastic quizzer with a heavy local accent, a West Country burr with a slight antipodean lift. That intervention prompted a little shuffling of tired bums. But a rather more significant announcement was to come.
paras.zh: “我还有一个给你，”一位热情的提问者用浓重的当地口音高声说道，带有一点点澳大利亚口音的西部乡村口音。这一干预让疲惫的流浪汉稍微挪动了一下脚步。但更重要的公告即将到来。

paras.en: Lewis Clifton, an assembly member who can date his family’s residence on the Falklands to the late 1870s, advised the islanders that an unprecedented economic war was being waged against them – a community no bigger than an English village – by a country of 46 million people.
paras.zh: 议员刘易斯·克利夫顿 (Lewis Clifton) 可以追溯到 1870 年代末，他的家族在福克兰群岛的居住地可以追溯到 1870 年代末。他告诉岛民，一个拥有 4600 万人口的国家正在对他们——一个不比英国村庄大的社区——发起一场史无前例的经济战争。

paras.en: “I am concerned that the level of Argentinian thrust this time has been at a different level,” Clifton said. “Perhaps a more vehement and belligerent tone than [seen since] 1982, because it has the potential to threaten our very economic development.”
paras.zh: 克利夫顿说：“我担心阿根廷这次的推力水平已经达到了不同的水平。” “也许比 1982 年以来的语气更加激烈和好战，因为它有可能威胁到我们的经济发展。”

paras.en: Facing a downturn in his domestic polling and with an upcoming election, Argentina’s president, Javier Milei, has legislated to criminalise companies and individuals involved in the Falklands’ nascent oil industry, and suggested the fisheries industry on which it currently relies for its prosperity could be next.
paras.zh: 面对国内民意调查的低迷和即将举行的选举，阿根廷总统哈维尔·米雷已立法将参与福克兰群岛新兴石油工业的公司和个人定为犯罪，并暗示目前其繁荣所依赖的渔业可能是下一个。

paras.en: The British forces capability at Mount Pleasant airbase – 1,800 personnel there and on Ascension island, four typhoon jets, a ground-based air defence system and with HMS Medway patrolling the waters – makes a military threat from Argentina largely hypothetical. But Buenos Aires has launched a full spectrum attack of another sort.
paras.zh: 英国在芒特普莱森特空军基地的军事能力——那里和阿森松岛上有 1,800 名人员、四架台风喷气式飞机、地面防空系统以及在水域巡逻的英国皇家海军梅德韦号——使得来自阿根廷的军事威胁在很大程度上成为假设。但布宜诺斯艾利斯发起了另一种全方位攻击。

paras.en: In response this week, Andy Burnham and his foreign secretary, Ed Miliband, restated the UK’s solidarity with the islanders’ desire to remain British, and promised legislation that might offer some protection against the financial damage imposed by Argentina’s economic sanctions. Interpol received Foreign Office representations suggesting they reject an Argentinian request for arrests relating to the dispute.
paras.zh: 作为本周的回应，安迪·伯纳姆和他的外交大臣埃德·米利班德重申了英国对岛民保留英国身份的愿望的声援，并承诺立法可能为阿根廷经济制裁造成的经济损失提供一定的保护。国际刑警组织收到外交部的陈述，表明他们拒绝阿根廷就该争端进行逮捕的请求。

paras.en: For the islanders, it was a welcome show of muscularity. They have never felt entirely confident in the spine of those in power back on the homeland. It was arguably the indifference of Westminster that led Argentina to launch its invasion in the first place back in 1982.
paras.zh: 对于岛民来说，这是一场受欢迎的肌肉表现。他们从未对祖国当权者的脊椎感到完全自信。可以说，正是威斯敏斯特的冷漠态度，导致阿根廷在 1982 年首次发动入侵。

paras.en: “I have never trusted the Foreign Office and I have been proven right,” said Norma Edwards, 84, whose husband, Roger, 80, a former Royal Marine, was attached to the SAS in the 1982 conflict. “Catching up time,” said Clifton, of what he saw as a belated toughness from London this week. But things remain precarious.
paras.zh: 84 岁的诺玛·爱德华兹 (Norma Edwards) 说：“我从来不相信外交部，事实证明我是对的。”她的丈夫罗杰 (Roger) 现年 80 岁，曾是皇家海军陆战队员，在 1982 年冲突中曾隶属于英国特种空勤团 (SAS)。 “赶上时间了，”克利夫顿在谈到本周伦敦迟来的强硬时说道。但事情仍然不稳定。

paras.en: The Falkland Islands might be described as a British success story. Four decades ago, there were 1,800 inhabitants, and its tiny wool-centric economy, 300 miles (480km) east of mainland South America, was dependent on UK government handouts.
paras.zh: 福克兰群岛可以说是英国的成功故事。四十年前，这里有 1,800 名居民，其位于南美洲大陆以东 300 英里（480 公里）处的以羊毛为中心的小型经济依赖于英国政府的施舍。

paras.en: Today the population, growing at 3% year-on-year in recent times, includes about 70 different nationalities, attracted by the 26% top rate of tax, good pay and opportunities in a growing and entirely self-reliant economy.
paras.zh: 如今，人口近年来以每年 3% 的速度增长，其中包括大约 70 个不同的国家，他们被 26% 的最高税率、良好的薪酬以及不断增长的完全自力更生的经济中的机会所吸引。

paras.en: There are Zimbabweans who came to de-mine after the war. Construction workers from South Africa who came to rebuild. Chileans who found something they liked after taking a Latam Airlines flight. The largest minority group is the Filipinos, who came to work in social care and the service industry in the late 1980s and 90s.
paras.zh: 战后有津巴布韦人前来排雷。来自南非的建筑工人前来重建。搭乘拉美航空航班后发现自己喜欢的东西的智利人。最大的少数群体是菲律宾人，他们在 20 世纪 80 年代末和 90 年代开始从事社会护理和服务行业。

paras.en: Working behind the bar at Groovy’s, a Nepalese waiter said he had come from Dubai. The money was better in the Falklands, he said, and “the people are nicer”. “The locals start at Deano’s bar, then it’s the Victory bar and here – then it is the Globe, for dancing,” he said with a smile. “After that they go to house parties.”
paras.zh: 在 Groovy’s 酒吧后面工作的一名尼泊尔服务员说他来自迪拜。他说，福克兰群岛的钱更好，而且“人们也更好”。 “当地人从 Deano’s 酒吧开始，然后是 Victory 酒吧，最后是这里 - 然后是 Globe，适合跳舞，”他笑着说。 “之后他们就去参加家庭聚会。”

paras.en: Such has been the Falklands’ success in attracting people that a permanent residency scheme, capped at 90 people a year, has been frozen for 12 months. The islands, for all their challenges, are somewhere people want to be.
paras.zh: 福克兰群岛在吸引人口方面取得了巨大成功，以至于每年上限为 90 人的永久居留计划已被冻结 12 个月。尽管这些岛屿充满挑战，但却是人们向往的地方。

paras.en: All of this had been made possible because of squid, said John Barton, chair of the fishing companies association. “It has been transformational,” he said.
paras.zh: 渔业公司协会主席约翰·巴顿说，所有这一切都是因为鱿鱼而成为可能。 “这是一场变革，”他说。

paras.en: In 1986, the UK allowed the Falklands to establish a 200-nautical-mile exclusive fishing zone in which those wanting to operate had to be licensed by the islands’ government. Licences sold to fleets of Spanish, Korean and Taiwanese “jiggers” have delivered major revenues, but the locals are increasingly running the vessels too.
paras.zh: 1986年，英国允许福克兰群岛建立200海里的专属捕鱼区，想要在其中作业的人必须获得群岛政府的许可。出售给西班牙、韩国和台湾“跳汰机”船队的许可证带来了可观的收入，但当地人也越来越多地经营这些船只。

paras.en: The islands’ gross domestic production per capita soared as a result, from about £2,000 in 1982 to £85,000 in 2025, putting the islands sixth in the world league table, just behind Norway. The tourism industry is also going strong, with 75,000 or more people spilling out of cruise ships every year at Stanley port, but that is at best a nice addition.
paras.zh: 因此，这些岛屿的人均国内生产总值从 1982 年的约 2,000 英镑飙升至 2025 年的 85,000 英镑，在世界排名中排名第六，仅次于挪威。旅游业也蓬勃发展，每年有 75,000 人或更多的人从斯坦利港的游轮上涌出，但这充其量只是一个不错的补充。

paras.en: James Wallace, 41, is chief executive of Fortuna, the largest fishing company on the island. It is a growing operation, which last year acquired Cornwall’s oldest fishing business, the Ocean Fish Group. But he is diversifying his business for a reason.
paras.zh: 41 岁的詹姆斯·华莱士 (James Wallace) 是岛上最大的渔业公司福图纳 (Fortuna) 的首席执行官。这是一家不断发展的企业，去年收购了康沃尔郡最古老的渔业企业 Ocean Fish Group。但他正在实现业务多元化是有原因的。
